title: Michael Penix Jr. and other Atlanta Falcons speak to media following practice | Press Conference
text: And Mike, how did you guys react to the news that the coach was going to inactive you and start the first week with the other two? He said, "How did we receive it?" Did they receive the news? Oh, yes.  Uh, yeah, we just talked to the coach.  The coach contacted us.  I had a conversation with both of them and, for now, I feel there are still things I want to improve on.  I'm sorry .  You know, obviously, just having that week of practice felt really good.  I felt very comfortable , safe.  But, hey, we still have a way to go. What obstacles do you think you have to overcome? In terms of strength, I feel like I want to be stronger.  I want to be stronger .  I want to be able to be out there and give the team 100%, and if I don't feel like I can do that, I don't want to... That's not fair to this team.  That's not fair to this organization.  I want to make sure that when I'm out there , I'm 100% and have no doubts in my mind that I trust my knee and that I can help this team win games. So, were you the one who had that conversation and said, "Hey, I'm not ready"? Did they come to you? How exactly did that happen? Yes, I mean, we were both having conversations with the coach week by week, just conversations between quarterbacks and offensive coordinator.  I feel like Coach D'Amato does a great job making sure he maintains a good relationship with the quarterbacks, and it's great to have that in a head coach.  But yes, I did have that conversation.  I just told him that I 'm not where I want to be right now and I want to be able to be 100% to help this team win games, and I'm very close, very close. So you feel like you're days away from that rather than weeks away in terms of being...? Yes, I mean, I don't think there's a deadline for that.  I feel it's more a matter of sensations, how I feel each day when I wake up, the pain I may feel, or how I react after an intense day and things like that .  So it is, it's all of that.    There really isn't a deadline for this.  But I know I'm very close.  I mean, I'm very, very close. How are you supporting Tua now that the first week is here and he's been absent this spring? Yes, I'll still be the same person I've always been, you know?  He's the starter and, well, we both play on the same football team.  I want to see this team win games.  So I'm going to support him.  You know, making sure to tell him about any play I see from the bench, anything he has questions about, I'll help him out, and, well, just being there for each other.  That should help this team win games, and that's what it's all about . Mike, is it hard not to rush back?  And obviously you've been through this before.  Does that help you not to feel that urge to be there just for the sake of being there?    It's not difficult, because I've been in this position before and I was in the situation where I rushed back, I didn't feel confident, I didn't play well and it didn't look good.  So it's like , okay.  I know that when I step onto that football pitch, I want to be 100% for this team.  And I know it won't always be 100%.  Every week players have niggles, knocks and things like that, but as far as my health and what I've been through, I definitely want to make sure I get to the point where I feel totally confident. How much does it influence the feeling that this is a critical season to prove yourself to this group and this coaching staff? Yeah, man, I'm proving a lot of things to myself, you know?  And at the same time, it's not about saying, "Oh , it's an important year for me," you know?  It's mainly about wanting to be able to give this organization, this team, 100%. And if I feel I can't do it, it wouldn't be fair to them.  And you know, I love this organization and I want to make sure that when I go out onto that field, I'm fully prepared. How has your last week been, Gerald?    It's been good.  Yes, it's been crazy , but it's been good. How did you find out that you were being switched to a different team? First my agent called me, and then Chicago notified me.  I was like, " How excited are you to be here in Atlanta?"    I'm super excited, man.  Obviously because I'm back in the South.  I'm from Florida.  So having that similar climate is great.  I'm super excited to be here. How would you describe your playing style? I like destroying matches, man.  I like it, you know what I mean? To create, you know, negative plays. Obviously catches, tackles for loss, all that kind of play. That's how I would describe myself, a party destroyer. How has it been integrating here, understanding Coach Ulbrich's system, and what has your relationship been like with the rest of the defensive line?    It's been good, man.  All those guys know how to play, you know what I mean?  They have helped me try to learn the system.  The system is really just going, I don't know if I can say bad words, but going to cause chaos.  So that's what I like to do.  Obviously, that's why I said I like, you know, ruining plays , entering the opponent's field and creating those tackles for turnovers and catches. So it fits me perfectly, man.  It's what I love to do.  I love, you know, getting out quickly, moving forward and making those plays. So, Coach Lolly has this attacking front that he has used for many years .  Exactly.  It was very effective here last year.  It seems like a very good fit for what you do. 100%. Yes. Why do you say that? Just like you said, a guy like me, you know, big, fast, strong.  If you push forward, man, you know , all that's going to happen.  So what he teaches is something I've been almost praying about every night, wishing I could just attack.  So being in a defense like this, where I can really go all out, is going to be huge What is your relationship like with Ian Cunningham? And what does it mean to you that he, you know, would like to come back and get you to bring you here? Yeah, it was huge, man.  Ian obviously played a big part in selecting me.  Um, and um, when he got here, I sent him a message, you know what I mean, congratulating him and stuff like that.  So it was great that he, you know what I mean, um, still, you know, thought of me.  And obviously he thought, "Holly, just leave me alone," because he made that exchange.  So , it was good, man.  Our relationship is good and hopefully it will continue to grow.  Is it okay to be, you know, like you have few Gators here?  We only have you, Kyle, and Juwan.    That 's enough.  That's all we need.  I was like, I think it was just me in Chicago, so two more is enough.  That's all we need. They have a lot of dogs here.  Do you agree with that? No, I don't agree with that, but we're...everything's fine. Hey, did you get to meet Grady last year? Yes, I did it.  Yes. Yes. Grady is amazing, man.  Grady is a great guy off the field, a leader , an incredible leader.  Um, I still like many of the young people who come in.  If you want to know how, do you know what I mean? What to do?  Just go and ask Grady.  Um, just because he's always in the right place, you know what I mean?    He is punctual.  He doesn't do many things wrong, so Grady is a great guy.  Um, he helped me a lot last year.  Did you ask him about the Falcons? Did you call him, like...? He was ready.  As soon as I said yes, he contacted me and told me I would love to be here, that the people were great and the city was great. So he had already contacted me. Yes, you all made the playoffs last year.  Two of his most recent teams have been in the playoffs a couple of times.  What's it like going out there to fight with him as quarterback? Yes, I mean, it's great. Obviously, as you said, he knows what it takes to win.  He's done it before.  It's simply going to require everyone.  Do you know what I mean?  Not just the quarterback .  It's going to require the whole team. Later in the year, you have to do all the little things right.  And that's what it's going to take. What has it been like to come back here, regain your health, and finally integrate with the starting lineup and that attacking line?    It's been a lot of fun, mate.  It's been a long off-season of rehab and stuff like that. But once I arrived, the physical trainers put together a good plan for me, along with the coaches.  And it's been great.  I've been enjoying it, shaking off the rust every day and getting used to American football again. You mentioned that you're from the south.  How has it been to be back here?  You're from Florida, but you're back on the southern side of the world. It's really fun, man.  Being back close to family.  I am very close to my family, so being close to home and having had my daughter 5 months ago is a great help;  It's great that my mom can come more often , and I'm also enjoying the weather. Congratulations.  They obviously named Tua as the starter this week.  We all wonder how his integration with them has been, and how much confidence that group of seven has in ensuring that he is ready? Oh, that was great, mate.  We have the utmost confidence in him.  We know he will do the job at a high level.  He has done very well since he arrived here. He had a great training camp too, so we're excited to see him in week one. With Tua and Mike at quarterback, how does that impact your job?    It really doesn't impact my work at all.  Since they're both left-handed, I'm still the blind side no matter what, so it's funny with both of them.  They are both great players. Is it different for you to reach a situation like this? How does your mindset change, if at all , after having been with right-handed quarterbacks? field marshal.    It definitely changes the game a bit for me, that's for sure.  I definitely need to be more aware of that. Especially when you're behind the quarterback, now that he 's a little closer to you.  So I just need to make sure I'm aware of that.  Make sure to keep the pocket space a little more than I'm used to. What has been your opinion on, uh, learning about this offensive?  Tommy Reese is coming to face the center and he's a new sensation.  It's new to everyone. Um, but for you in particular, trying to prepare for this offensive. Uh, that's a great scheme.  Uh, a big offensive.  I feel they also have a great selection of plays.  They position us as players to succeed.  So, um, you know, we just trust them and when they call for a play we know we have to go out there and execute it well.    I know the offensive line always goes out to dinner on Thursdays.  Have you already chosen where you'll go this Thursday? Uh, not yet.  Uh, but I'm sure it will be , we'll probably know where we're going in the next few days .  Yes. Your last year in Florida, uh, was in 2018, right?  That's when Kyle arrived, right? Do you remember how quickly he stood out? Uh, Kyle stood out from the moment he arrived on campus, man.  He always showed many flashes of athleticism and has always been an intelligent guy with a high football IQ.  He knows the game like the back of his hand.  So it's always fun to come back, you know, and be able to play with teammates I had in college. Have you changed as a person since 2018 ? Oh, no.  Not at all.  It's still the same KP.  Great guy overall, great teammate, excellent in the locker room. Going back to what you were saying about Tua having a large camp.  We were talking to Tommy Reese, I think it was last week, and he commented that he felt Tua really took ownership of the offense and how it works. How have you seen him do that in the last few weeks? Oh, he's definitely taking control and you can see his confidence levels increasing every day.  You know, he keeps us going as an offensive, you know, he's keeping an eye on us.  He makes sure we are attentive in the meeting, and attentive when leaving the meeting.  He is confident when making his calls, etc.  So we love that. Any trash talk with Janell so far? No, not yet.  Not yet, but I'm excited to see it in week one, for sure.    I did n't know if that's, you know, Coco line pride. Yes, yes, yes. Something like that, a bit of provocation. Yes. No, not yet, my friend, but I'm really excited to face him again. Yeah.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 1 Media Availability | Monday, September 7th | Press Conference
text: All right. Finally, game week. You know, we're we're excited about uh the opportunity we have in front of us. Uh so, today what we'll do uh is the guys came in, got a lift. Uh we're in meetings now. Go out in the practice field uh and really work situational uh ball. So, working some red zone, uh some two-minute, some team drills uh on special teams. So, some good work today. And then we'll come back in this uh afternoon and and really turn our focus towards Pittsburgh. Uh obviously, we've had one eye on them it feels like for since the schedule came out. Uh but, start to really hone in on the Steelers. Uh obviously, I have a ton of respect for Coach McCarthy, that organization. It's it's a uh you know, they're the division champs, reigning division champs. So, we will have our work cut out for us and and as you can imagine, we'll focus on our work um this week. And uh there's a lot of work left to do. Uh and I know it's game week, but we'll make sure that today's uh a very productive day towards our goal for Sunday. And then, obviously, get into our true work week uh Wednesday morning. Um as you guys saw the the uh report, Tua will start. Uh Cooper Rush will be the backup. Mike Glennon will be inactive. Um really really proud of those guys. And I told them this this morning. I think those guys have worked like crazy um all off season. And they've pushed each other and they've supported each other. And that's what we'll do uh for Tua. We'll we'll continue to support him. Um and and and understand that this is a a a collective group that is is constantly looking to help each other. So, uh really enjoy that group, proud of them for what they've done, what they've been able to accomplish, and and continue to obviously move forward and and help our football team uh this week versus a very good opponent. But, with that, I'll take any questions. >> What was it ultimately that led you to the Tua decision? >> You know, I think every decision I make for the football team, you're taking in all the information available to you and sometimes information changes and and you know uh certainly with a decision like this, you want to make sure that you're you're you're uh taking all the information from the spring to the summer to how people are performing. Those type of things. So, um felt really strongly uh about this group and and feel good about where we're heading. >> Is Mike just not ready? >> Yeah, Mike is getting better and better and better and I'm very proud of him for again and for how far he's come. Uh but this will continue to be uh something that we are work together with Mike. We're all on the same page, which is is great between myself, Mike, medical, uh you name it. Uh everybody feels good about where Mike is heading um and he'll continue just to work like crazy and and that's his focus and I think he's told you guys that. He's uh he's going to focus on trying to get better every single day. >> How much was that part of the decision that Mike just returned to practice fully 2 weeks ago and didn't play in the preseason, etc.? >> Again, it goes back to just, you know, making the best decisions with all the information available to you. I think Mike had six uh 11-on-11 practices if if it if it was that. Um and he he did a very nice job. So, he's continuing to get better and better and and you know, I can't overstate uh how how proud I am of Mike and and how he pushes and and gets you know, what he's put his body through what what you put your mind through when you're going through these uh injuries and those type of things. So, he is continuing uh to get better. >> Was there a chance you thought he could get back over the course of the last week or why why else would the delay till now be >> Yeah, I I think again, um it goes back to uh every decision you're taking in information. So, of course Mike just getting back to 11-on-11 wanted to make sure we uh you know, gave him an opportunity in in these practices and we did but uh feel strongly about uh our decision with everything all the information available to us. I guess the best way to put it. >> When healthy, do you anticipate him being your backup? >> I'm going to really stay in in week one right now and in in Pittsburgh and and not speculate past that. I don't think it's fair to anybody at this point. But feel feel good about where everybody is. >> When was this decision like you know firmly decided on? >> Over the last week, I'd say. >> Michael continue to be fully go in practice. >> Yes. Yes. >> Is it more his his mind? Like is it just trying to make sure he trusts his knee? Is it is it that aspect of it or is it >> I don't think it'd be fair for me to speculate. I would tell you he's doing everything in his power to get ready. And and that's all the work he put in the training room, all the work he put in the weight room, the work in the meeting room, out on the grass. So he's doing everything that he needs to do. >> With Tua, I mean, where does your confidence come from with him? >> Yeah, I've gotten to see Tua work from again the spring till now. New system for for all these guys. And and like I told them, you know, there is a lot of newness with with our players, with coaches and you know, everybody getting up to speed. And and he's done a really nice job of working at it. So confidence for us as coaches and players comes from just doing it on the field and and watching guys continue to work. And I think he's really put himself in position to to go be the best version of himself. >> At the risk of belaboring this point, because he's on your 53, he could be your third quarterback without costing you a roster spot. So does that suggest that he does not feel ready to play a game right now? >> Yeah, I would tell you Josh, I don't want to speak for Mike. I'm very very confident in the plan that we have for Mike. With myself, Mike, all the coaches, medical, we are all on the same page with this and feel really good about where he is at this point and will continue to work with him today, tomorrow, moving forward just to when he's you know, to get better each day and and will I'm not going to put a time frame on that. I don't think that's fair to anybody. I'm just going to you know, focus on on what he's doing day-to-day. >> Kevin, is this purely a plan just for this week, this regular plan? >> Similarly, as you guys can imagine, I'm a blinders person. I got the blinders on so I see week one in front of me and after this one then we'll start on the next one and those type of things. So I don't think it's fair to to really go past this week on anything related to our football team. >> What have you seen from Tua coming back in that last preseason game and then in the practices and such? >> Yeah, I I I think obviously I've seen Tua back since April and and and so I I like I've told you guys before these evaluations of players and these type of things are all encompassing and I know uh preseason games can get a lot of the attention as well they should but I've gotten to see him work really really hard throughout this entire process of learning a new system, learning his teammates. So much of quarterback play uh comes you have to know your teammates and you got to know how this receiver comes out of this break versus that receiver and where does this guy want the ball and so there's a lot of nuance I would tell you that goes to to playing that position. I think he's done a really nice job getting on the same page with all those guys. >> Tommy mentioned building a of weekly plan based on kind of what fits each quarterback's eye. Is there something clarifying now in this decision for y'all to start prepping? >> Certainly and that's something that we as coaches have been thinking through go all the way back to April. You know, and I've told the quarterbacks this really doesn't matter the plays that the coach likes, the coach, offense coordinator. It's really with our player, our quarterback, the guy with the ball in his hand is most comfortable with and there's no shortage of plays in the game of football. So, what we'll do and we have done is make sure that when those quarterbacks get those plays coming in their ear, they feel really confident because they they know that play. They know the why behind the play. That they know what the intent of the play is and I think that's where Tommy and and coach Van Pelt do an excellent job with our quarterback. So, certainly with Tua, it's it's no different. You want to make sure that the concepts in the pass game are are ones that he's comfortable with and some of those ones that he's comfortable with are new concepts per se to what he's done in his past. So, that's where I appreciate Tua and and and Mike and all these guys learning a new system. There's there's some new plays that come with that and if they're plays that fit their minds eye, if you will, then then then you keep working them. If they don't, you move on to the next one. >> We saw the the rookies kind of grow and develop throughout the preseason. What's your philosophy on first-year players and contributing kind of like right out of the gate? >> Yeah, I I think the old days of of guys redshirting and and you'll see them in a year, like that's just not the reality of the NFL and I've been a part of it where rookies play and they play a lot early and that's where I'm confident in the group that we have. I'm confident in in the coaches and in putting the plan together for our players to develop and we'll see as week one rolls around what those roles look like knowing that roles certainly evolve as the season goes on, but yeah, I think we've got a rookie class that has been extremely diligent about their work and and now the fun part where they get to go play the play these games. >> I have a unique state situation for both these coaching staffs trying to scout a team who has a new head coach and you guys are doing that with Mike McCarthy and vice versa. Just what is that process like trying to kind of go back and see what they've done in the past and obviously things will be new. >> Right. >> Is there with the new offense? >> Yeah, no shortage of tape because you have, you know, you got the Steelers all of 25. You know, Steelers have done a great job on offense, defense, and special teams over the years. You have coach McCarthy coming in with great success from Dallas days, from Green Bay days with with Aaron Rodgers. Brian Angelico is the offensive coordinator coming over from Minnesota who's done a nice job. You have PG, Patrick Graham, coming from Las Vegas. He's been in different stops over his career. Have a new special teams coordinator, you know, so we've studied you're studying all of that film and also you have to make sure as coaches and certainly what we filter down to the players that you don't overburden them with all that tape. So, I think in week one of the season, I think coaches are excited when it goes to week two and you have tape to watch of what it's going to look like because, you know, you can it's impossible to watch all that tape and prepare for all of that. Now, do we as cuz we're crazy people watch a lot of it? Yes, but it's our job to to make sure we give our players a plan and then understand as much as it is about your opponent who you respect and is a great opponent. It's also about you and how you perform, how you execute on on a lot of what you've been working so hard on over the last few months. >> And to that point, too, when you talk about the staff, you know, they're coming in from different places, but you're extremely familiar with the personnel. How much of a challenge is it kind of scouting both of that where you know the players and you know the coaches but just haven't seen it? >> Sure. I mean, there is week one's there's the element of the unknown everywhere. Certainly, I know a lot of their players just from over the years. They have new players like all of us all play all teams do as as you go year to year, but they have great players and they've got great players along the front and the back end, you know, on the perimeter on offense. Obviously, the quarterback's one of the best ever do it. So, understanding the personnel is important. I can speak to a little bit of of my history going up against the players and and but understanding that it is week one and in a new scheme, new system, quote unquote, so there may be some changes to to how they've been used in the past and again, it's easy message then for your players to as much it is is about your opponent and you have to learn so much about your opponent. You also need to make sure that you have your own stuff in order if you will and make sure that you're performing at a high level because of your execution is is is on point based on all the work we've put in again since April. >> Going back to the final preseason game, you said afterwards you were pleased with some of the operational stuff that Tua did with the offense in those couple series, but ball security was an issue. How have you seen him kind of progress or address that, you know, in the last couple days and where's your comfort level with that? >> Sure, as everybody knows ball security is is paramount in this league and turnover margin is the number one stat that there is in in the NFL and and I can promise you all 32 teams are preaching to take care of the ball on offense and take it away on defense and and special teams as well. So, we'll continue to to keep that a emphasis of everything we do. No different that for the quarterbacks and and the centers or the running backs or anybody who's touching that rock, a punt returner, kick returner. Doesn't really matter who you are if you have that ball, we'll be all about our technique in those situations, but that'll always be our focus every single week. >> You mentioned last last month about how Campbell was a huge for you trying to install the run game. How much did you learn about your guys about it if your line can move well enough to handle everything? Do you like the flex you have there? >> Well, it's I think looking at offensive football period, you know, run game, pass game, there's so much that goes into that. When you talk about the pass game, it's the protections, it's the concepts, it's it's your pass catchers. When it's the run game, it's the concepts, it's what your runner see runners see well. So, a lot of what we've been doing especially since the pads came on what understanding our players and and understanding uh what schemes will fit us best. Now, you you can't run all of those schemes in week one, but certainly I've found out a lot about our offensive line, our tight ends, our runners, our wide receivers. So, all all of those guys play such a huge part in in the run game and I know it's easy to say, "Hey, hand it off and and and let the runner do his thing." Well, everybody's got to be on the same page. Quarterbacks have to get you in and out of the right play. They have to carry out their fakes. Receivers have to buy in and then execute in in the run game. And I think if you look at our receivers and you think look at any good run game around the league, there's receivers blocking and and there's guys that are you know, getting that what could be a good run, you know, called a 6-7 yd run can be a 16-yd run because a a receiver's doing his job down the field. So, it's a huge emphasis for us and I think since the pads came on in training camp, I do think we found out what have worked find out what fits us best. Also understanding that it's a a long season and and you're going to have to pivot throughout that season. >> Unlimited might not be the right word for it, but do you feel like you've got enough where you can kind of, you know, adapt in the season if you have to? >> I do. I feel strongly about our players. Feel strongly about our coaches and it's not easy. It's and certainly versus the Pittsburgh Steelers it's not easy. But, there's things that you have to try to execute in a given game plan and and understand also that each game plan is going to be a little bit different. >> Time for one more? >> What's Jessie Bates' status heading into the game? >> He's practicing. Yeah, ready to roll. >> O'Leary? Go ahead. Yep. >> Can Can you kind of explain cuz there's been some confusion about a player in this with regards to Mike being healthy versus kind of being ready to play? Can you kind of talk about from a coaching perspective >> Sure. >> where or just like how you cross that divide? >> Well, I I think it's every it's a case-by-case basis. We have guys that are coming off of injury that are still working through it different injuries. Some are ready this week, some are ready that week. I think it's important for us as coaches and and an organization to understand that's a case-by-case basis on how guys that the readiness to play based on where they are in in their rehab if you will. Um when it comes to players you you can get cleared for 11 on 11 or you get cleared for a game, but then you have to be able to do your job and I can think of you know offensive tackles over the years that sure you're cleared but to play, but are you are you able to function at the level that you need to function at and whether it is because of a shoulder injury or whatever. So, that comes up every week with us and our players and and our medical staff do a terrific job and and I feel really strongly that that we're on on the same page with all of our players understanding that the time frame for each player is a little bit different and and we'll always work with our players, with our medical staff to make sure that we're making great decisions for our players which ultimately will be great decisions for our football team. Okay, thank you guys. Appreciate it. Thank you.

Um, he's played next to Cooper BB, he's played next to Gayton, so that's nothing new, the communication and all this stuff. He actually gets a ton of reps with those guys anyways because we manage uh sizz in some in some areas. Um but uh at the end of the day, like I said, uh you know, we tendered him the way we tended him because we trust this guy's a football player and uh he's a damn good football player that unfortunately is just playing behind a lot of really really good players and uh so we have great confidence in TJ. >> Then which thumb is it? >> Uh I think it's the left. Yeah, I think it's the left. >> John Michelle with the Athletic. Uh how much more does it put on Cooper BB's plate and Tyler Giden's plate to have him out? N I mean again Tyler Smith's a great player, but again offensive line play is tied together, you know, and um like I said, we've gone into games with four new starters on the offensive line and uh again I think you know I'm very very confident that this group will play well against a really good front and um you know uh I have great confidence in in in TJ Bass. you know, he he's extremely bright, uh, very physical, great athlete, and so, um, again, he'll do a marvelous job for us, I'm sure, stepping in. >> Then what does game planning this week look like with you and Christian, and how does that differ than maybe how you and Matt Eber were last year? Yeah, you know, I think we've got uh we've got scheduled a little bit better, you know, John, in terms of, you know, the times that we'll spend together, you know, whether it's Tuesday, you know, u midafternoon, just kind of getting on the same page about some stuff and then tying it together on a Friday and through a Saturday. And so, we've got some things scheduled that maybe Foo and I didn't. I think that's part of the evolution and me learning. It's always better to have something on the schedule so it's, you know, not impromptu and hey, I need to go figure this out. Um, so really excited. The one thing about Christian I love is he overcommunicates that stuff. He just wants to make sure that I'm getting what I need to feel good as the play caller and the head coach to know exactly what's going on with the defense. >> Nick Harris for start telegram. Was there a moment it happened with Tyler in camp? >> No. Uhuh. >> Yep. >> You've talked about this right tackle situation. Is that something you want figured out by week one or is it kind of just an ongoing thing? >> Yeah, again I think you know it's one of those things that's going to be ongoing. I think you know Terrence Steel um is a starting right tackle right now. Broadick's here learning, doing an awesome job learning. And um you know, I think one thing we've done is we've gotten a lot more athletic uh overall as a offensive line unit. When you look at, you know, Brick coming on board, you know, you know, coming on board, and um I think that's a good thing for us. We've got, you know, some depth now at tackles, Drew Shelton, I think, is going to be a really good football player. Um and, uh, you know, again, we'll see how the the week goes and we'll see how the numbers play as we carry the eight offensive linemen. you know, we got to figure that out throughout the week and we've got time to do that. But, uh, uh, really like what Brick's done coming in, learning the system and, uh, again, very, very, uh, unique athlete when you watch him move and play and do those things. >> And what do you make of the Giants off seasonason obviously a lot of change up there. >> Yeah, they think they've done a really nice job. Obviously, you starts with, you know, getting coach Harbaugh, uh, terrific coach, a lot of respect for him. Uh, but they've spent money and resources. And you look at their front, you know, very experienced, you know, from the inside out, DJ Reer and, um, you know, some of the pieces they have in there, Shelby Harris and, you know, Brian Burns a great player. And then they get, you know, Tmaine as as a mic linebacker, uh, Arvel Ree. Very talented group. And, uh, again, we're going to see talented groups each week, but they've done a nice job. >> Tommy Arsh, Dallasways.com. Jonathan Bullard looked like he was back today. What do you expect him to do? >> What number was he? you remember? >> Very good. You guys do pay attention. Nice. Yeah, number 90s. Thank you. I wasn't sure. Uh, no, he did good. Yeah, he's been uh, you know, he's been kicking ass in rehab, Tommy, and uh, feels a lot better. And, uh, it's been great to see him back out there. >> I think so. Based on today, we'll see if he has, you know, any pain or anything tomorrow. But when I talked to him, uh, during practice, he felt really, really good. And then as the offensive play caller, when you're going up against Guy Dard, who has been a defensive coordinator, but not with this personnel group, how do you balance watching what he did in Tennessee last year and looking at what the Giants did with some of their guys this year? >> Well, number one, Dinard and I go back to St. Louis. Uh, I've known Dinard was a good coach for a long time. I was a coordinator when he was, I think, the assistant secondary coach, assistant DB coach. Might even had a title, safeties coach back then. It's going way back 2011 or 12. Um, damn good football coach. Uh, he knows what he wants to do. The secondary base, you know, drives it. You know, they're a bunch of shell defense like we see. Really good job disguising, very multiple. Um, and he's got some really cool pieces to use. So, uh, this is one of those games that, you know, you don't want to overthink. You know, you're going to kind of do what you do. They're going to do what they do. It's going to come down to execution and, uh, probably going to be a pretty close game in the fourth quarter and, uh, see who can finish. >> Scott Dixon with the AP. Do last week. Basically, it does feel differently this year in terms of positive vibes, but those don't win you football games. I'm sure you agree with that. And and how do you preach that? And maybe does the Tyler Smith injury sort of remind everybody that, hey, we still got to go out and win games? >> Yeah, I think, you know, it's easy to talk, Skyler. I mean, we put our goals out there for the world to see and hear and debate and uh it's okay. It's the way we want to be because we do believe in ourselves and we have a lot of confidence. you know, injuries are part of the game and uh like I said, you know, I think the what Dak's talking about with all the positive vibes is real. And uh again, I can't predict how this game's going to go. I can't predict how the next game's going to go. Um you know, like I said a couple weeks ago, if we have to win games 10 to three, I'm good. I just want to win. And we have the type of competitors in this locker room that believe that as well. And I think they believe we will find a way to win um you know, a lot of games. and uh it starts this week, but again, we got to get through Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and put together really good week of practice. >> How much does the hiring of John Harbaugh sort of get the attention of you and maybe the whole division? >> Uh I mean, the guy deserves tremendous amount of respect. I mean, the run that he had in Baltimore, I mean, my old man said, you know, 10 years is a shelf life for a coach and what was he 16, 17 years? Um great man, great Christian. Uh I just I love the way he lives his faith. My faith is really important to me. I have a lot of respect for him and how he lives his life, but guy's a tremendous football coach and uh us coaches, kids, we all kind of get along. >> Joe, Joe Hoy, Dallas, you guys hosted Arbell Reese for a visit. What do you remember about the scouting process with him and how much can that actually help you in terms of now knowing him, but knowing where he went to as well? >> Yeah, I mean the speed and the the power and the urgency that he has in his body is unique. I mean, big man that runs fast and um can make up for, you know, maybe an eye violation or two because he's got so much makeup speed, but uh dynamic player. Um they've got a uh you know, a really good group around him of veterans to help him. You know, again, talked about Tummaine Edmonds and you know, Burns and Abdul Carter going into year two and the safeties are veterans and so uh really good football player. Ohio State, as you guys may have witnessed this weekend, they uh they got a lot of good football players and uh we're fortunate enough to have a really good one on our team as well. on Caleb DS and >> he's obviously got edge capabilities as well. They've invested a lot in their pass rush from an outside standpoint. In terms of trying to game plan against that, how much does that keep you on your toes and how essential is communication then against a front like that in terms of pass rush? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, we we're not going to be surprised if they blitz him if they walk him to the edge. Uh he's a a very good pass rusher. the speed is unique like I said and um you know but we've got things in in our holster that we can use to try to make him you know maybe be confused and that's what we're going to try to do but um I do remember that you know guy was a very very diligent worker and had a lot of respect for him. So um you know appreciate the player and look forward to competing against him on Sunday night. Babe, >> Babe Loft, Cowboys Radio 105.3, The Fan. Uh, two-part question, but I only like to ask one question at a time. Great. Uh, you guys led the league in 10 plus play drives. Um, obviously the analytics are all over big play scoring increases almost doubles if you're over get a 15 yard play in there. So when you look at those 10 plus play drives, is that a good thing for you or you know defense want to make you drive have a 10 play drive? Sure. So how do you look at it? >> Uh I think it's always easier to score when you have explosives. You know we look for explosives. Uh teams, you know, have a way of trying to take them away. But what I love about our team, our our quarterback, I'll start there. Dak's ability to process information and if people are playing really really soft, check the ball down underneath, take what they give us. Um, you know, we're pretty aggressive when it comes to third and fourth down, certainly in certain parts of the field. I think that's part of it, but, you know, I think it's a compliment to be able to say you can go 10 plus plays and score touchdowns. It means you're in condition, means you're mentally tough. It means you uh, you know, understand, you know, it's one play at a time mentality. And, uh, I think that that's a good thing. you know, we're we're fast and we're explosive as well, but uh I think we take pride in the fact that we're able to do that. >> And then the followup, uh you also take pride you had the fewest three and outs of any team last year in the NFL. >> Is that that's a big deal? >> Yeah, it is a big deal cuz you can't if you get a three and out, you can't get those 10 plus play drives. Um again, I think it comes down to the players, you know, I mean, their ability to execute, Dak's ability to convert third downs, the people we have protecting Dak, the weapons we have on the outside. Um, again, we don't, you know, talk enough about, you know, what Javvante does without the ball in his hands. I mean, the guy's a terrific runner. Scored a ton of touchdowns last year, but this guy's a pass protector, is unique. Um, and so, uh, the big thing for all of us is we want to live in third down imag. You'd love to not have a third down. You know, you'd love to avoid third down altogether, but, uh, from a third down standpoint, we were really good last year in third and six or less. And like the rest of the league, third and seven plus is is tough. Patrick. Hey coach. Patrick Berlescowboys.com. You guys revamped the defensive coaching staff, rebuilt the defensive roster. Um, you're hardressed in looking at your schedule to identify any week. I mean, in NFL you can't take a week off nonetheless, but you guys are going against a lot of impact mobile quarterbacks, some physical guys like Scatterbo in the in the back field. How long realistically do you think or are you looking for this defense under Christian Parker to to gel, find its chemistry, find its, you know, its unity and be able to be disciplined against these guys? >> Well, I just want to see them play hard. You know, Patrick, I think they'll do that. I think the play style has been evident throughout the preseason without our vets. I think, you know, the one thing that, you know, if you talk to CP about, you know, the play style is real. We've got speed, you know, at every level. You know, Jaylen Thompson's fast. Dwy, maybe he's one of the fastest linebackers in the league. He can really run. Demo obviously great speed um you know so when you have these athletic edge pieces that's one of the reason why you invest in a guy like Malachi Lawrence you know they can run and and all that so um that's where this game has gone you know a lot of these mobile quarterbacks that are athletic and um they can extend plays and they can beat you scrambling they can beat you throwing Jackson Dart does a great job you know when he gets out you know scrambling and scrambling to run and making plays and keeping things alive and you know we got to be really good with our our uh pass rushing integrity and keep them in the pocket. But um the team speed on defense does help us. >> And keeping to the defensive side of the ball, what's you guys's plan for Von Miller and his ramp up? Is he trending toward playing against the Giants or how does that look? >> Yeah, I mean I think he is. I think, you know, we haven't finalized that. Today was a bonus Monday, so we're really just kind of getting them exposed to some of the basic concepts that that they do offensively, defensively, and special teams. Uh but uh in terms of play time and the roster numbers and all those things, we'll we'll finalize that. But I don't see any reason from a [snorts] uh physical standpoint that Vond wouldn't be ready to play this week and um if he's one of the guys that makes it, then he will. But we haven't had those discussions yet. >> Gel, CBS Sports. Brian, you said after last year you wanted to kind of take a different like holistic game day approach to you being the head coach in year two. kind of how do you anticipate what you do on game day being different than your first year here? >> Yeah, you know, I think it starts during the week, Garrett. I mean, I think game day will be different because the week's going to be different. You know, like I talked about to John's question, I think, you know, I'll have a better idea going into games what what the plan is on on defense, certainly on special teams. And uh I think you know one of the things we're going to do it's a little bit different this this year is kind of have a you know a meeting later in the week with the coordinators talking about you know hey how we think the game's going to go. You're always ready to adjust but u we can kind of anticipate you know hey okay we're thinking this on offense. How does that affect the defense? Defensively they're thinking this. How does that affect special teams? Special teams is thinking this. Um it allows you to get ahead of some things and uh we didn't do it last year. Uh, and part of the evolution is it kind of helps you go in with a mindset of how you think the game's going to start, but as always, the best coaches and best teams find a way to adapt as the game usually doesn't unfold how you think it's going to. >> How do you how have you seen Jackson Dart adapt? Um, I guess maybe preseason limited, but a lot of people criticize him for taking too many hits when you're going up against a quarterback who likes to extend plays to the point where maybe you can get some shots on him. What are your thoughts? I love the way the guy plays, man. I think you see the the team loves the way he plays. Um, you know, I think, uh, guy's very athletic. Uh, you know, I think they've done a nice job pairing him with with Matt Naggie. Um, you know, Greg Roman, they've they've you got some things that fit them from the RPO game to the way they want to use some of the quarterback run game stuff. Um, so again, it goes to the fact that, you know, they're going to have a number of things for us that we haven't seen. What do you do? you trust your rules and they're going to be in a 11man formation more than likely quarterback plus 10 others and might be three on one side, you know, two on the other, but as long as within the rules, I think we'll probably be able to get lined up and uh it's going to come down to who makes plays. >> Ed worker, WFAA. Um, last year obviously you guys gave up the most points in the league on defense and have done that over the last two years, but if as you anticipate you can trust this defense in a way maybe you couldn't last year, how does that affect the way you strategically manage a game and offensively call plays? >> Yeah. Uh, again, Ed, it's a good question. I think it's it's fair. You know, we don't really look back, but like again, I feel very different about this defense going into game one. uh doesn't mean that, you know, we won't have, you know, big plays given up here or explosive run or a blown coverage. That's going to happen week week one early season football is usually that way. But, um, yeah, I'm pretty comfortable that as I'm planning to call the game and even on game day, I have a sense of kind of what's going on on the other side of the ball. Last year was not a very good year for us defensively, so it was easy to be in an aggressive mindset. But like I said, I'm very comfortable playing 10, seven games and field position and um you know, we just want to find ways to win and uh I think like I said, the three units that we have that we'll put out there on offense, defense, and special teams give us a chance to do that. >> Christie, >> Christy Scales, I wish radio 1053, the fan, you were talking about play style of your defense a moment ago. Going to flip it and ask about the Giants with Harbaugh taking over. Um do you believe that a team takes on the identity of the head coach? How quickly can that happen? And then what do you expect their identity to be? >> Uh I think they're going to win with preparation. That's what, you know, John's all about. You know, I mean, he takes a lot of pride in the preparation part. I think we all talk about that, but I think, you know, talking to people that have been on John's staff, he does a great job kind of like we're talking about today, staying in the moment, trusting the process. Wednesday's Wednesday. Don't skip Wednesday to get to Friday or Saturday. Um and uh you know, the guy knows how to win. And so again, I think uh uh they've uh they've had a really good offseason just like we have and now we get a chance to go compete and uh you know play 60 minutes or 60 minutes plus whatever it takes in a really cool environment uh on Sunday Night Football. Okay. >> Have you made a decision starter at corner? You've been either or uh Durant and >> Yeah. Um we haven't decided. It's based off of packages and plans. Obviously, Caleb gives us a lot of uh versatility. Uh but you'll see them all play. Doc, >> I talked a little bit about Dak's ability to process info. What do you make of that? And you ever thought of how many decisions a quarterback has to make in that 40se secondond span that you guys have? >> Yeah, there's a lot of decisions. Uh yeah, I think he's uh awesome um at, you know, just handling, you know, lots of information, uh down in distance, uh personnel, uh defensive personnel, formations, motions, things like that. Um and I think it speaks to uh the benefit of having a veteran, you know, being a guy that's been in this system for, you know, almost five plus six years, whatever it's been, uh with, you know, Kell and Mike and myself. Uh, I think that's important. But, um, yeah, I mean, it's amazing how much he can handle and do it in a short period of time. That's why people don't, >> [snorts] >> um, you know, probably talk about, you know, they say some people say the hardest thing to do is hit a baseball, which I can't hit one, so I'm not saying it's not, but playing quarterback's got to be up there, man. Uh, these guys are um on a time clock against some of the best athletes in the world, and they have to process a lot of information. and they got to bail us out when we make shitty calls and um so it's a Babel attest to it. It's really hard. Nick, >> how do you expect touches to look in the running back room behind Javvante? >> Uh you [clears throat] know Javvante's our bellcow and uh you know the other guys are certainly going to play, but uh you know Javvantee is one of those guys that you know the stronger he gets is based off how many carries he gets. And what we think we learned with Javvante, it's more about how we handle him during the week, Nick, in terms of his workload during the week, not so much on game day. Um, but again, you know, in terms of rotations and things like that, we have them finalize that stuff. You know, we're getting ready to once I get rid of you guys, I'm going to go get started on some stuff and um, you know, got some decisions to make based on special teams as well as we build the 48. C, >> you haven't made a decision that was going to start opposite blend, but how does Rebel look to you this this entire camp and even preseason? >> Yeah, I'm excited. I'm excited for Von. You know, I think you see a guy that's got a lot more confidence than he had last year. Understandably so. Uh last year he was limited. This year he's been really full go. Uh I think like I've said, he and Dererick Ansley are a great fit for one another because they're both, you know, the technique matters. Um you can tell by when he goes up and presses, cut splits and things like that. Uh, guy's a good football player. So, I think his mentality and mindset's way different than it was last year. He's always had skill. He's always had traits. Um, but again, you know, they've got, you know, some talented receivers. And, um, I think the one thing Bond's learned is you got to have a short-term memory because, you know, literally you're going to give up a play and next thing you got to go play defense again. >> How did Beckham McTom in the preseason? >> Yeah, he's still a good player. I mean, you know, guy uh knows how to get open, knows how to play. Um, ton of respect for him and what he's done in this in this league. Uh, I thought he's fine. >> All righty. >> Thanks, guys.

title: Zac Taylor Press Conference - September 7
text: Forward. So, regarding injuries, how are the three of them for tomorrow?  Uh, referring to this week. All three of them were good today.  So we'll wait to release the injury reports on Wednesday, but I was encouraged by the progress all three have made. The captains were named today.  What was the process like for choosing the boys who were selected? Yes, the players vote for them, and I think it's a good group.  I think this year, probably more than any other, a lot of boys received votes.  Many boys received a good number of votes. The seven were clearly the chosen ones, but it's a very good group offensively, defensively, and Evan as a specialist has had a great camp.  So I think we should prepare ourselves to be guided by them. There are many other young men I will also ask to lead us.    It makes no difference whether they are captains or not. I think we have a very strong group of guys on the team who can really help us move towards where we want to go. How important is that? Is that what you and Duke were building when you put the roster together?  Obviously, you need talent, you need skilled players. Yes. That next level of leadership, of maturity, all of that. Yes, I think it influences every position .  When you have a real veteran who can lead by example and is willing to help younger players with things that the coach won't always be able to help you with.  You know, there are times when they're focused on another position and you have a veteran in the role who can take a young guy and help guide him and point out some things.  I think it's fundamental, and when we really have that in every position on our team , it's very good for us and for the coaching staff to be able to have other guys who can be coaches on the field and help bring out the best in everyone we have on the roster.  Did you see any prominent examples of that during camp? Yes, I saw them.  Yes, that's how it was. Absolutely.  I saw a lot with the defensive line.  I saw him in all positions.  I think those are the ones that really stand out.  But I really think that from beginning to end we have a very good group of guys who want the best from everyone, because they know that's what will give us the best chance to win. From a purely football perspective, how did you see Dexter change the defense while you guys were playing? I saw him in training. You just have to pay close attention to it.  You know, we dealt with that throughout training camp. When we face our defense, I don't want to go into too much detail, but he affects almost every play.  And it gives the others a great opportunity for individual duels that they have to take advantage of, and they have.  So it really opens up the game for the other 10 players on defense.  And also find ways to isolate it, you know, not just have it absorb double marks all day.  If you can leave it to a one-on-one matchup, that puts a lot of pressure on the quarterback and the offense, so the coordinator has to focus all game on: Where is he? Is he inside, is he outside? Who else is on the field?  So I think it gives us a lot of opportunities to succeed on defense. It seems like every team has a real player on the defensive line, but how many players in the league actually require double-teaming?  Like those players who have to be marked by two at all times. Oh, you're putting me on the spot, you should have written to me to think about it.  Well , on an interior level, off the top of my head, I'd say between five and ten players, where you really focus on the interior defensive lineman when preparing the game.  I think you could name a higher figure at the extremes, but internally it's a problem because the pocketbook shrinks and you have to adjust your protection plan for deceptive plays and third chances. Is Vita Vea one of them, and how do they approach it? Yes, he's a great player.  You have our full attention.  He has been a tremendous player for a long time.  I think it's helped our infield players to face Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, and all the guys we have there.  They are all unique in their own way, but he is a tremendous player .  He has our utmost respect.    You ask me a lot about Dexter and pinners, but what exactly does Daron Payne bring to your high school that you might have learned? Obviously, you knew what kind of player he was when you got him, but what have you learned about what he can do, not from a leadership point of view , but purely from a footballing one ? He has a high football IQ.  So that does help from a leadership point of view.    I know he said not to say that, but it helps, and as far as communication goes, that helps the other 10 guys. I think he's a very good tackler. So that's fundamental for anything that goes beyond the third level or if he reaches the second level.    He does a very good job of taking down players.  And I just think his knowledge helps with all the cover and disguises and all that kind of stuff, but he's earned that captaincy because I've seen it in him. The way he leads by example, the way he leads through his communication, has been truly fundamental to the development of our defense. What does it say about the defense that they, Brian or them, came up here and earned the captain's appointment so quickly? I think those two, Boye and Jonathan Allen, haven't been afraid to come in here and lead by example.  And to speak, I should say to speak.  And they earned it through their play in training camp and their preparation during the offseason, but they weren't afraid to come here and just earn their voice a little bit. They know they've earned their voice through their play, that's why they're here.  That's why we paid them that money, that's why we selected those boys to come here and help us.  So it's good for me to see that they're not tiptoeing around all this; we don't have time for that.  We need to get started now.  And their voices, along with other guys, Jordan Battle and all the others we have. DJ Turner has really amplified communication in our defense and how it's evolving in a very positive way. Jamal and T obviously know this offense, but how important is it to have them available and in practice on the first day of the first week? Those are two leaders, for example.    I mean , I know T is a top leader on this team, maybe he doesn't wear a C on his chest, but in my mind he does because of the way he's helped everyone on offense and the whole team.  I would say with the corner players.  So having those guys leading the way there is really good.  We have a really good group there.  Dre has been here for several years, so he does a great job.  I feel it's a very well-rounded position for us in terms of knowledge and experience in our system, and they are always willing to help the young people with their training, their assignments, and everything that is expected of that group.  They've been doing it for quite some time. You mentioned DJ Turner.  How have you seen him evolve as a player and leader I think, honestly, from the last training camp and throughout the beginning of last season, he earned his opportunity as a starter, and once he got it, he made the most of it, covering some of the best players in the league and taking on that responsibility, becoming someone we can rely on;  And now, in this off-season training camp, he's taken that to another level.  I am very proud of him.  I think he has absolutely earned the opportunity to be captain.  He is one of the best cornerbacks in this sport.  He is a leader on our team.  He's someone who, sometimes, when I felt the energy on the training field was low, I could hear trying to cheer everyone up, so we'll count on that and he's completely earned that right . You've been on both sides these past few years.  What do you think of the concept of quick starts and mini-games throughout an entire season?    I mean... It's something to talk about, you know, that 's all.  It's a topic of conversation before the games have actually been played.  So there's nothing to talk about because we haven't put anything tangible on the field yet.  Therefore , there is nothing to criticize or praise regarding the system, the players, or anything else.  So the only thing left to talk about is the quick start: will you achieve it or not?  We plan to give it our all and these guys will be ready when we take the field on Sunday.  I'm excited about the atmosphere the fans will create in the first week.  I can feel the enthusiasm of our followers.  The "all orange" event , I think, is a great way to start.  We are renovating one of the walls in the coaches' offices and we are going to put up a picture of our stadium when our fans really made it vibrate .  I have great memories of that stadium when our fans are fired up;  And, obviously, we have to give them something to cheer about.  But I expect a tremendous atmosphere that will give us a big advantage in the first week, with Tampa arriving here, and we'll take full advantage of the crowd noise. How long has it been since your last match and what has it been like to be at the point where you can play again? Yes. That's a good question.  It feels like some time has passed.  You know , it was... I won't go into details about last year.  I feel energized right now .  Our boys are ready to begin.  We feel we have a good plan in place. Speaking of the fans last year, their request for the first week was to make sure no one went up the escalator.  Do you have a message for the fans for the first week of this year? that match.  It was a great job of technical direction on my part.  So it's the same thing What is the main key? Last year we were on the brink of disaster too many times.  What did you learn last year to ensure that... there's something that can be salvaged? What 's the first thing? Try to start quickly or something like that? Being fundamentally solid in every area is a basic element of the first week.  Generally, the battle of lost balls will decide the result when you have two really good teams.  Tampa is a really good team to start with.  So all those details you preach about situations, fundamentals, and ball security will be reflected in the scoreboard at the end of the game. Generally, at the beginning of the season you can point to some of those statistics and they will tell you the story. There is always that balance.  You know , I think even with a returning group, every year is different, so you do everything you can to make sure you're prepared for whatever they might throw at you, whatever we might throw at them, and make sure the players have confidence in what they're doing and understand that in the first week, 100% of the game won't go the way you want.  There will be things you'll have to adapt to and respond to, and some adversity that will hit you head-on , and I'm excited to see our guys respond to that part.  That's really the key part.    It's not just about all the good things we do.  It's about how we respond to something on the field and in the bank if it doesn't happen the way we want;  I think I know what I'm going to see, but thinking about it is one thing, and actually seeing it is quite another .  Thank you.

title: Matt LaFleur: 'Every year is a new challenge'
text: We have No. You guys will find out eventually. We're going to put something out. >> Okay, but you did elect to do the captain thing. >> Yep. >> Did you guys expect Harrison Smith was going to be back off of that this year? >> Yes. >> Okay. Um What challenge does he still present? >> Oh man, that guy I kind of refer to him as the straw that stirs the drink. I mean, like he's out there his command his ability to get them in and out of calls it shows up all over tape, but I also think they they've got a lot of smart players and you can see cuz that that scheme presents a lot of different challenges. Um and so you I think the only way to do it is you better have some guys that can handle all of it and they do a really good job with that. >> You faced Brian Flores a lot, [clears throat] but what are the challenges starting a new season when you don't necessarily know what >> That that's it. That's it for everybody everybody in week one. It's I think the early part of the season is always a a big challenge. And hopefully we've done a good enough job of presenting our team whether it's offense, defense, or special teams with a a bunch of different looks to get them prepared for that moment. >> Hey Matt, when you get to this point on the calendar, how much of your game plan do you have already in place going into a week one compared to other weeks where you might be doing it in the week? >> Yeah, I would say there's a significant chunk. I think in every phase. You know, just especially we just had 3 days or whatever, but even prior to that you're kind of you're kind of ear marking and and making notes and you get a long time the whole off season really to prepare for that week one. >> But how does that make this week different? I mean, you're obviously practicing [snorts] the game plan like you would in week two on, but it's not the same. >> I think you get a little more sleep. I mean, cuz you're so much more you're so so more prepared for it. So, it's it's a normal week. It's I mean, especially I'll to speak for myself, I use every second I can making sure that every play that we have in in the plan is I don't want to call it foolproof, but you want to try to avoid as many hurdles as humanly possible. >> Matt, what was that dichotomy like for you mentally? Like, you feel more prepared than ever with your plan, but you also don't really know the un-scouted looks you're going to see on the other side. >> Yeah, I mean, that's just it is what it is. And that's why you have rules and you got to go back and follow your rules. And certainly, I think they do a great job in all three phases. Their special teams is one of the best in the league. They they're they're very aggressive unit. I think offensively Kevin's always done a great job of putting guys in position and then couple that with the fact that they got I mean, they got some real superstars over there. Got a new quarterback that has always been a challenge to go against and his ability you got to defend both elements of the play. You got to the initial element and then the off-schedule piece. And then defensively just with the amount of pressure that they love to bring. I mean, it's just it's tough in all three phases. >> Matt, at what point in the week do you guys decide who if anybody you're going to elevate from the practice squad for that week? I guess the reason I ask is that I would assume you'd want to get those guys some reps >> Yeah, absolutely. That's something that we every week's a little bit different and certainly there's going to be times when you have you go up to game time and you just got to find ways to get whoever potentially could be up enough [snorts] work that they feel confident to go in the game and perform at a high level. So, but typically we like to do that early in the week. It certainly helps I would say our team's coaches, you know, making sure that the right people are in the right spots and you're not I don't want to waste any reps on guys that might not even be in there or are in a different position. So, the earlier the better, but sometimes you can't [snorts] always do that. >> Matt, you guys you guys you've gone against the Vikings and O'Connell obviously a number of times. >> I think this is our third time opening up at Minnesota. >> You you know his offensive system and whatnot, but in recent years it seems like you're preparing for a different quarterback like every time you face them. So, what's what's kind of the challenge with >> Yeah, I mean it is a challenge and I think I I've got a lot of respect for Kyler and his ability, like I just mentioned, his ability to play on schedule or off schedule. He's got a great arm. He's super elusive. But yeah, I think every year is a new challenge. You got new pieces, new players. Certainly we have new coaches, especially on the defensive side of the ball. So, every year is a new challenge. >> Third time opening in Minnesota, is that good, bad, indifferent? >> Well, yeah, I mean it's I think opening day there's you could feel it last year when we opened up at home versus Detroit. I mean it it's got a playoff type feel. The intensity is ramped up. There's a lot of unknown. So, I do think earlier on in the season it tends to be a little bit more of an advantage. >> Are you guys going to have Banks and Babatunde healthy? >> We'll see. >> Either way, how much of a strain has that put on you guys preparing an offensive line with them missing so much time to this point? >> Yeah, I think it you know, you talk about continuity. It's hard to get build continuity if you don't have five guys out there, but it is what it is. We're not the only team faced with those circumstances and you just got to got to try to make the best of it. >> Two more, please. >> I'm sure every coordinator goes through the game plan process differently. With JG now, this is your first week. What What have you noticed about the way he does it and anything stood out about it to you? >> Uh I just think he's he's ultra prepared. I mean, he puts a ton of time in. He has all off season kind of prepping for for especially the early portion of the season. Um but he's I just I'm amazed every day just sitting by him and and hearing how he thinks and how he sees the game and I think he's he's as good as anybody. >> And now when Stacy Dales and Brian Baldinger were here and you said what you did about Jordan at the line of scrimmage and Stacy's like, "Well, wait, you coached Aaron Rodgers." >> You just had to ask Aaron Rodgers question, didn't you? >> [laughter] >> Um I'm curious just if you could kind of encapsulate how far Jordan has come in that and then the other part of the question is how on point does he have to be this week when you're going against Brian? >> Yeah, and and to add to that, I would say then you got to deal with the crowd noise cuz that is a loud environment as well. So, it's it's pretty chaotic. But I think he um to watch where he came from to where he is now, I don't know if anybody would have guessed that he could come that far and that's a credit to him. Certainly, I think it was a benefit not having to be rushed into it and you build up a bunch of scars. Um you know, and getting to sit back and learn from a guy like Aaron, I think was [snorts] extremely beneficial. I think that's a big reason as to why he's been able to do that at such a high level. And but he just it's not a surprise to me um in regards to how even keel he stays throughout the course of a game and certainly you got to make split-second decisions and some of these looks are really tough and you're not always going to be right, but what what's been so impressive about him is just he has a plan. So, like if it's not right, he knows how to get the ball out of his hands. >> Is Is Is Florida's defense as challenging as anyone in the league when it >> I would say so. Yeah, absolutely. I think just cuz I mean, you're going to get pressure. You know it. You just don't always know where it's coming from and they they do a good job of um just putting people in certain positions and I think it's it's complex on offense. I think it's easier for them. So, he he's got a really good system. >> Hey, what did you think of last night's college game here? >> Oh, that was cool. That was That was pretty cool. The atmosphere was electric. I wish it would have been a closer game, but it kind of got away in the second half, but um yeah, it was it was it was pretty cool. I just didn't love all the wear and tear on the field, but it is what it is. >> Have you checked it yet? >> I have not. I have not. I'm sure Allen's out there right now getting it getting it tip-top shape.

title: Game week! Texans stand up for QB1, captain C.J. Stroud, Kayshon Boutte role vs Bills, injury update
text: people um you know have this narrative of us as athletes like we're not humans like CJ's a human at the end of the day like none of us are perfect. We play this game. Not only that he gets, but just us as NFL play. >> Hi guys, Aaron Wilson at Reliance Stadium as the Texans continue to dig into their preparations against the Buffalo Bills. One of the top matchups of the opening week of the regular season. So, you think about the Texans in this matchup. Obviously, they have to contain Josh Allen. You have to tackle running back James Cook III. And they have to get these guys blocked on defense. They have Greg Roso. They have Bradley Chub. They have a good linebacker, Terrell Bernard. Occasionally bring him on fire blitzes. And they have a very good safety in Cole Bishop. So they also have a new defense coordinator, Jim Leonard. That was part of the conversation with Deco Ryan today. Jim Leonard, they've had to dig into some old tape things he did at Wisconsin, Illinois to kind of understand some of the things that he goes about in building his strategies. And it'll be interesting to see some of that. But the real headline matchup obviously is the Texans defense, the top ranked defense against Josh Allen after sacking him eight times last season in 23-19 victory with Davis Mills under center. This time it's going to be CJ Strad. And before we get into a lot of matchups, I want to talk about the team captains. So they vote on these. This is balloting from your teammates. And they voted CJ Strad a captain. Now the other captains, they're on defense. It's a Zizal Shire. It's Will Anderson Jr. And it's Nickel Jaylen Petri. And for CJ to be named a captain, that's significant because it's a testament to how your teammates feel about you. And I had some conversations today. I asked some questions about CJ. As you guys know, he's endured some heavy criticism ever since that Rocky performance against New England Patriots. No immediate contract right now. There's still he could have one, but that's pretty much on hold. would be surprised if they, you know, raise their offer significantly enough for him to forego what he could get, which is a lot more money with a strong season. But in talking to Ed Ingram and he said he is absolutely tired of CJ Stra being dunked on. He feels like CJ is a great quarterback. And Trent Brown also talked about CJ and know he says heavy is the head that wears the crown. you know, being the, you know, being in that top spot. And also, Aranti Ursery said he sees a lot of growth from CJ as a leader. So, just some interesting comments from teammates. And you can say, well, Aaron, they're biased. What are they going to say? They're going to grip him. No, but it's how you say it. It's how supportive you are. That's where you read between the lines. Look for those nuances and emotion. And that's where I, you know, picked up on something just today, listening to those guys talk about CJ and that stuck out to me. So, I'm always kind of trying to take the temperature of the locker room, listen to things, hear, well, how do they perceive this? What's the impact of something? So, to me, that was interesting. He said he couldn't name four better guys if he tried. So he says they're consistent in preparation. They care about the locker room. They're courageous when it's time to speak up and that's what you want as captains. He said the team selected those guys and they represent us very well. Jaylen Petri said is very significant to him to be a team captain and big thing is to win. Have an injury update for you. Trent Brown, it's not his thumb even though he wears the brace on his thumb. It's actually an old wrist injury and it's been lingering for a while. It's something he has dealt with in the past and it is not expected to impact him at all his availability or effectiveness against the Buffalo Bills. is something that, you know, is enough for him to wear a brace, but didn't need surgery. So, repeat, no surgery for Trent Brown. And even though it looked like a thumb injury because of the brace he was wearing, it's actually his wrist. All right. So, wanted to get that cleared up.
