>> We'll see. >> Uh what do you make of the Lions? >> Lions are a good football team um you know I think they got a ton of talent they've obviously played some really high level football for a number of years now really well coached and um you know that's going to be a fun environment you know that place uh what they've done uh in Detroit they've created a really really challenging environment for everyone to come into that place at Ford Field to play and um it'll be a lot of fun for our guys our guys will be excited about it. >> Is St. Brown as good of a test for Yonas some of getting used to a new position as you could have in week one? >> Well I'd say he's one of the premier uh receivers in our league um you know he obviously plays a lot of time in the slot but he can play all over the field his versatility um his route detail his ability to catch the football in contested situations his run blocking is as good as anyone in this league um you know I think a lot of receivers in our league can learn from him a lot of players can learn from him and so uh it'll be a fun test. >> When they have injuries like they do like at safety is that kind of like you go in test and then adjust as you get information like how how do you approach that when it's kind of a little bit of a blind spot? >> I would just say week ones, there's going to be an element of unknown for every team. Um It's about playing really good football, really sound, clean, fundamental football and um you know, we've had a whole off season, they've had a whole off season. They're going to look a little different, we're going to look a little different. Um you know, there's some personnel things that um you know, they've known for a while that, you know, we're going to have these guys or we're not going to have these guys and so again, these guys have had a lot of success uh as a football team and so uh they they know the type of formula that needs to be uh successful in this league. And so uh it's going to be a really fun game. >> You've said a lot of it just like pull from a lot of your different stops to kind of get your coaching style. So like is there anything specific that you took from your time in Detroit that that like you know, you've kind of implemented here or within your just your scheme or anything? >> I was there with Jim Schwartz, Jim Caldwell. Um Two uh two different approaches to being a head coach, to be honest. Uh both really successful. Think the world of both of them and uh you know, I had a great time. I mean, that was Detroit's kind of got a little little soft spot for me just from the standpoint of it's kind of my first time uh Julie and I were married and we're kind of out on our own. So uh it's um it's a fun place. It's really cool to see what that organization has done uh over the course of the last few years of kind of developing one of the, you know, most competitive teams in our entire league and they've had tons of success and Dan's done an incredible job of building that culture and that environment and um there's just seems to be an incredible alignment uh with everyone there. >> How does your job change when you have a second-year quarterback with like 10 career starts? I mean, do you do you care about the responsibility of developing more as opposed to just implementing and and like, you know, taking a longer-term view as opposed to, you know, um installing a playbook? >> I just say I mean, our quarterbacks are still young. Uh you know, Tyler's obviously, you know, the guy, but um it's still a young group. There's still plenty of football to learn and grow from and improve from a fundamental and technique standpoint. And so we're still on a journey of of growth and I don't think that stops anytime soon. Tyler's done a really good job of applying himself all off-season. Um We still got we still got opportunities to grow and we'll continue to do that. >> Have you developed a coaching philosophy? I mean having having been a young quarterback in the league and then a coach at different stops. I'm sure some people take the idea of development more seriously than others and and like have you decided what what you want your philosophy to be on that? >> I just think there's continuous growth. You do have to keep stacking as you go and I think that comes with continuity in the system. I think you have to be at the end of the quarterbacks have to be able to play very free and confident on the field. And if we give them too much, you know, you can over analyze football very quickly and easily. And so I think that's always kind of having a a gauge level thing of seeing where the quarterbacks are at, giving them enough tools to be successful on the field, different things they can get in and out of, but at the same time allowing them just to trust yourself and play play clean football. >> Do you find it easier or harder like to not present them with too much when it's week one when there's so many unknowns but yet there's also like all this film you could or like you know, all this history you could incorporate? >> Yeah, week one I mean you can over analyze week one more than just about anything just cuz there's so much unknown to it. Again, both teams have an entire off-season to reimagine what they want to be and so I think week one so many times you can watch we all watch these college football games all week and high school football games all week. And I mean the fundamentals and the techniques and playing clean football I mean it just showed up every single game. And that's what this thing's going to come down to. There'll be some schematic things that will be new on both sides that you just have to react to. But Um you know, you got to just play >> What was your Boise State review? >> [laughter] >> I was bummed. Uh we hung in there. We were close. Uh had some opportunities. Uh yeah, Wazzu was the same thing. So, it was a little bit of a bummer bummer weekend, but I was proud of both teams. >> Um Jonah was released with a non-football illness designation. Is that something that's already been cleared up or is that >> Yeah, we're we're aware of it. Uh all good. He's he's here. He just got in uh I believe this morning or last night. And so, uh yeah, he'll be good to go. Obviously, um you know, everyone was aware. >> Is he able to practice already and then is he >> they're just going through the medical thing to see the timeline for him. So, it should be shortly. >> There's kind of like a a lot said last year about island rate for your your tackles. Is that kind of like an overblown thing? Like is that like check and release kind of maybe changing those numbers to like that rate? >> Yeah, I I think it's it's something to always assess. Um you know, there's there's pros and cons to having guys in help in protections. And so, um especially when you play premier edge rushers like we're going to play week one. And you got to be conscious of those things. And you know, again, I think it's how many times the you put them in those hard downs. You know, it's just like we talked about quarterbacks. Quarterbacks have hard downs. And uh some play designs have hard downs for tackles as well. And so, you got to be conscious of that as far as, you know, how quickly the ball's coming out. Is it a screen? Is it uh does it have some help to it? And so, uh you know, while while we love loved our two tackles, they're two of the best in this league. They're going to be really really good for a long time. We still got to be conscious of it. >> Is there a way to get them like help though like where you're kind of checking and then cuz you guys are like check and release numbers like are they pretty high compared [clears throat] to the rest of the >> Yeah, I think so. I think um you know, any time our tight ends and running backs can have some awareness to that, I think there's certain play designs. And a lot of times we talk about understanding where you are in a progression and uh the timeline of that. When you're on the back side of something, you know, you're four or five, you probably have a little bit more time to make sure everything's secure before you get out. >> What do you see the focal point for your team going into this season? >> Yeah, I think I think it's just, you know, again, playing our brand of football. I think so much of it comes down to the fundamentals and techniques early in the early in the season. Uh a play style. I think we need our guys to play fast and free and aggressive and um you know, just that relentless effort. And so, uh if we see that and you know, we keep improving the the cleanness of the football, we're going to play some good stuff. >> Feel any different going into week one than you did last year? Like, I don't know if you were nervous last year or anything like anything from an emotional standpoint? >> Um first games are always fun. They're always fun. They're always exciting. Uh there's an element of unknown, which is uh an exciting part of it. You know, I think all of us at this point we've practiced a lot. And so, uh it's time to play a play a real game and uh evaluate yourself and then shoot, there's a whole bunch more coming. And so, it's all about how you respond after that week and week out and uh there'll be plenty of corrections coming out of this game. And we'll just have to get better. >> I mean, you can only you can only play the games the way that they're scheduled for you, but I'm just curious about the the wait till till the home opener. Is there a value in building that anticipation for you all or like how do you is there a thought process behind that at all? >> I don't know. I mean, been in this league long enough to have done different schedules where you get to play home early and get have to wait a little bit. Um you know, it'll be fun when we get home. Ultimately, we all love playing at the dome and uh it's a special place. And so, uh we'll have to wait a couple weeks, but uh you know, we'll be ready when we do. >> You see the Michigan game? >> Did. >> For a second or >> I have not seen the uh the uh mythical camera. So, or like clock. So, >> until until until we get verification on the uh mythical clock, we'll uh I'll side with the 0 seconds. >> Fantastic. >> or, but you know, given you're in Detroit, like the the fact that the Lions are like annual contenders in chief right now, at least I know that they didn't make the playoffs last year, but like the fact that they've really built that up and like you could kind of tell what that means to the the city and all that given you know >> Yeah, Detroit Detroit's an awesome city, a resilient city. Um yeah, I haven't been been there in a number of years. I think the last time we played there was 2019 uh if I remember right, when I was in in Dallas. Um But it it's a really cool place and uh you know, I think credit to Dan and their organization of really building out a plan and um you know, it took a little bit of time for them and uh sometimes that's that's what happens in this league and um credit to their leadership, just the patience it took to kind of keep developing it, keep getting it right, and then um everyone saw a couple years ago the way they finished that season, they had a ton of success, they had a lot of confidence coming off of that, and so uh it's continued the last few years, and you know, it's a really good organization. >> How do you go about piecing together sort of the evaluation of their offense with the players they have, but a new offensive play caller who hasn't who's who's called in the NFL before? Like how do you go about that, Herbert? >> Yeah, you're going to have to look at two different types of film. You're going to have to naturally look at Detroit, and that's the players that that that group has had a lot of success doing certain things together, and so uh certainly I don't think they're going to stray away from that too much, but there's going to be some assets coming from Arizona that they're going to get to implement, and so uh you know, you think of it I've I've done these moves a few times, you know, in my career where you come come into a place like a Philadelphia where there's a ton of success, there's a lot of good going on, and um you don't want to lose all the good in a transition, so they're going to try and hold on to that, but there'll be some new pieces coming from Arizona, and so uh it'll be a fun battle.

title: #Saints T Kelvin Banks, DE Carl Granderson & RB Audric Estime on preparing to face Lions in Week 1
text: You're too for how is the difference between this year and last year for you? >> Uh I mean I say the biggest difference is that I'm not trying to like I wouldn't say play catchup, but like I'm trying to like I'm not trying to learn a playbook or or uh just learn different stuff as I'm going. So just understand that stuff's going to happen and when it does happen you just got to can't focus on that specific play. He's just like you said, you just got to go out there mono mono and play ball. >> Are you you expecting about 50/50? >> Say it again. >> 50/50 on like him going >> Yeah. left and right. But he does play both sides, so I I expect 50/50 >> when you have three joint practices against three good teams. So I think it's going to be a test for our defense and I think we're going to be ready for that test. So um we're going to show the league what we're about um since football and play fast, play hard, and play together. >> I know you just want to you just want the ball right before the game. title: Aaron Brewer, Zach Sieler, Patrick Paul meet with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: So, going to ask you about the guards next to you. Where do you think Jonah is a better player this year and has Kaden been about as good as you thought he would be making the transition to guard? >> Um Jonah, I feel like he's better in all areas. Overall pass game and run game and just IQ of the game. I feel like he developed a lot. And KP, he's been just on greatness as we've been playing this whole time. Like he man showing so much brightness and upside in his run game, his pass pro. And everything looking good and even in the one preseason game like we played all together as a full unit like we put together a solid drive. And so now it's going to be the actual season, so it's a little different from training camp and preseason and OTAs, so after this first game we'll really be able to see where he at. >> What's the specific skill with Kaden that you think will make him a good guard as long as he plays guard? >> His size and his like his size and his speed, man. Like he has an athletic big dude. Like you don't see people that big be able to move how he move. And so just with that in itself he can do a lot of big things in this league. >> You've done the captain thing going back to last year, so you know you were expected to to still be on there. What did it mean to see a Patrick Paul be on there for the first time? >> Uh you know, I'm just very excited for my guy, you know what I'm saying? Definitely us both coming into Miami together. Like his rookie year was my freshman in Miami and so just to see him from his rookie year develop into the guy he has and just gain the confidence and grow into the leader he has become. Like it's just so dope to see and witness his whole journey. >> Drew, this is obviously a season opener. Does it feel like more than that with the start of a new era or do you kind of keep it chill and a season opener is a season opener? I say season opener is a season opener and but like it's it's a new group, you know what I'm saying? We got a young team and just new coaching staff, man. So I say it is a little more, but it's it's still the first game of the season and you know me personally like nobody believing in us right now and so I love that. I know I love that as I love haters and so I put that on my back and walk with that with my chin high, you know what I'm saying? >> Speaking of that youth, just what will that demand of you as a leader in 2026? >> Um just to give everybody just the same recipe of the game, you know what I'm saying? Every successful team every successful player, every successful coach just always preaches that effort, that focus, the confidence, the detail, the technique and so I feel like that's the biggest thing to preach throughout the season just for a successful football team or just a career player or coach those are the things you have to focus on and so just to keep preaching those things and have people to literally that become their identity and yeah. >> Who are you guys going up against Max Crosby on Sunday? You going up against a ton of elite defenders, Michael Parsons, etc. Do you want the offensive line to be on edge and you know Max is here, Max is here or do you want to just kind of be chill and we'll just rely on our training and don't make a big deal about it? >> Um I'd say it's a little bit of both, you know what I'm saying? Like you have to acknowledge a great player when I it's a great player. He's he's one of the elite rushers in the league and so you got to respect his game but also don't make it bigger than it is. Like he's he's still a player in this league and you're a player and so when it comes to that have a confidence in your training and what you know your technique and your effort. Don't do nothing more than what you've been doing. And so I feel like that's the recipe when you going to get some elite player. >> When you were coming into the league as as a young player, rookie, what was some of the best advice the guys gave you? I'd say one of the biggest things like people kept telling me is how to prepare, your preparation. And also just being proactive with my body and so like you come in young a lot of dudes you see a lot of young dudes, they don't have like a solid recovery routine or just a a preparation routine. And so like them two things was a big thing like they always co- like emphasize to me. Like they saying like you can be in this league as long as you want to, but if you're not taking care of your body, your body not going to be able to take care of you. And so I think those are two biggest things is staying in your playbook, coming up to games, like how to prepare for games, how to study for games, how to watch film, like those were the biggest thing. It wasn't really a lot of things that they talked about on the field. It was more stuff off the field. Yeah. >> Who sat with you and taught you how to watch film and how to prepare how to prepare for Sunday? >> Ben Jones. Yeah, he was a center at Tennessee when I came in. He vet and Georgia guy. He was I think he was about like year seven eight when I came in, but he been around a while a little bit. But he was like one of the smartest guys I've I've been around. Like when he was playing center, he was making all the calls for everybody across the line. Like he could make the calls for the defense if he needed to. And so just saying he operated how he went about things from walk-through in the meeting room, how he prepared for games, like he was a person that sat down with me and just literally taught me like oh this how you look at this. And you're going to a game where you watch the first down, second down first, runs to the open side, runs to the close side. Then you go to the third down. Like he taught me the whole breakdown of how to dissect this NFL game. >> Another veteran uh who you were with early on Roger Saffold in in Tennessee. Kevin Proctor told us that you put him on his film to watch. Why was he a player you wanted KP to to study? >> Uh I think just one their size, their strength, and just like the energy they have. Like if you ever see KP, he always bouncing around, he moving like he a young guy, you know what I'm saying? So he got a bunch of energy, he just strong and quick. And so if you ever watch Roger Saffold film, like he was so strong, but he was so twist up and like he was probably one of the best run blocking guards I've ever watched, you know what I'm saying? Like he used to take guys out of their cleats, that's 320 lb guys, like elite guys photo and so I see KP and how he move and how like he just his his body and like his makeup like I can see him being that exact same way. Like he can be so dominant in the run game and so that was the guy I really want him to study and dial in on. >> What part of Malik's leadership style and how he sort of evolved since you knew him as a kid? Um do we maybe not see or hear with our own eyes what's going on behind the scenes? >> I say he developed as a leader one because when he came into Tennessee he didn't have that leadership role. He was coming in behind Ryan Tannehill and then it was Ryan Tannehill team, Derrick Henry team and as such. And so like now that he have do have that position I see him like he has the same character but good thing about Malik like he's he keep he stays level-headed through everything and so that's someone you want in the midst of chaos and when things going left or right or off like he stays level. And so I feel like that's a great thing that Malik has and one of his abilities to do. >> You have a lot of guys on this team who are going to be playing their first real NFL game on Sunday. >> Mhm. >> What was that experience like for you? Are you going to tell us you were cool or were you nervous? >> No, I was cool. It was the same thing even when I went into college like I had to tell myself that I don't never want to make no moment like bigger than it is cuz once you start overhyping yourself you start making little mistakes that you shouldn't make or just doing things out of the ordinary because you making the moment too big for what it is. And so now I feel like you just need to have confidence in what you do and believe in yourself. I think that was the biggest thing when from our freshman year at college start even to my rookie year start. Like I've practiced with these guys. I've seen these dude. I watched my film compared to their film like we the same players and so we nobody out here has superpowers. We all human and so that was just the thing I reminded myself going into my rookie year. And so I went into it with much confidence, prepared the right way and went out there and played with >> So, Zach, I'll I'll ask you what I've asked a couple of others. Um obviously, this is the season opener, but it's the start of a new era also. Is it a typical season opener, or does it feel a little bit bigger? >> Man, I mean, you just got to play each week it by itself, right? But like it feels great to be able to get out there and finally play football again. I mean, what's been since January for us? So, um you know, guys work around all off season on improving their game, figuring out what they need to do better in the spring, and working on that, and then working with the new staff, and all these guys bring to the table is incredible. So, to be able to go out there and uh finally showcase that is very exciting, but you know, it's week one, right? It's exciting across the league, but you can't um over hype it and get too worked up, and you know, make little stupid decisions. I'm I heard y'all talking about the college game. I mean, you saw all the stuff that went on around this league uh the league. Um stuff like that happens, and you can't let that happen. So, um some not to be long-winded, but some we preach is, you know, you can't beat yourselves. So, making sure all the little details are honed in on, and we're focusing on those things from uh practice from day one is huge to uh I guess uh beat that curve early. >> What is it like to have half the locker room between the ages of 22 and 24? >> Uh it it's it's definitely uh over the years been, you know, seeing the different ages come through here. Obviously, guys like Klay has come through or uh Mostert, uh Cardona last year. Um it it it's it's really it's honestly it's refreshing um this year with these guys and seeing >> [snorts] >> all the energy they bring, and they the right mindset is the biggest thing where you got young guys, but they don't act young. Um a lot of them act very mature. They're locked in, focused, asking the right questions, how to see the game, how to work this, what to do here, how can we better here, and uh it's exciting. You don't see a lot of the uh young guys that are running around and excited to be in Miami for what most people think of Miami for. So, >> You could be like a mentoring big brother to a bunch of the young guys. Do they ask you off-field questions, how to handle money, stuff like that? Have you gotten much of that? >> Uh couple, yeah. Um you know, and honestly, I mean, well, look at the NFL now, right? Kids are coming in with money. Um so, it's it's it's really trying to help I mean, I tell them any ask me anything, open book. Um you know, I I I've lived this life and been here for a 7 8 years now and uh in in Miami and uh learned a lot. You know, I've made mistakes and I'll I'll openly tell them and own up to them, you know? What's a man without his mistakes? Let me try again. So, uh yeah, I'll tell them anything and they ask the right questions, again, like I said, so to help out in any whatever ways I can, I love doing that. >> Without saying, obviously, who asked you anything, was there one interesting or unique question that you said, "That's a good question." That off-field advice. >> Well, the fun one, uh J-Rod asked me about aviation. So, of course, that's a fun one for me now, so I think he's kind of connected in the aviation world. I don't know for sure now, but >> What does it mean to be named a captain for the third straight year? >> it's an honor to be named three years now. Um to be a captain and then I I think it's earned every year. It's not something that should be given. It's not something that just just cuz you were last year, you should be it again. Uh so, to me, to earn that again this year is a huge honor. Um to see the new locker room, the new guys to still think that of me is a incredible. So, very blessed and uh not going to take it lightly and and I think half hit on it earlier today where it's like, "Hey, look, the captains we're going to push you guys harder than everybody else cuz we expect more of you." And they absolutely should, so I'm excited for this year, new career this year. >> Four years running for you, how much do you like to see the the new guys come in and and be like the like Patrick Paul, Malik Willis who just came in as a captain, T. Von finally getting it? >> Oh, it's great. Uh to see Malik come in um from Green Bay come here and just with the confidence and just the energy he comes in with um is incredible. Uh so, to to see that absolutely um love seeing Malik do that. Pat Paul is another great example of a guy that just working from the ground up. He's been here, he's worked here, he's made his career here and to see him earn that and he has earned that is incredible. So I'm very excited for him work alongside him >> and same with the rest of the guys. So >> Zack, what's the unique challenge of going up against a team in week one when you don't really have any film on them and then they also have a new head coach? >> Yeah, I mean I mean kind of sounds familiar, right? So the big thing with week one is I mean know your opponent, you know? Guys in the old line, guys in their offense, guys in their defense uh they've played in the league before. I mean yeah, you can get you absolutely should and can improve in the offseasons but there's still tape out there. So to to watch each guy individually and then watch as a whole what they do or what their mindset is or was in the past. Those those tendencies are going to carry. So um so to to be able to do that and find those little details absolutely but obviously it is different than call four, five, six weeks into the season where you have a few weeks of tape built up. >> At what point did you learn how to study film in your opinion properly and also >> COVID >> COVID. Absolutely. Um I was watching film but I was watching it. I was watching it like a like a spectator. Um I wasn't watching the little fine details um and then COVID happened and for me it was a big blessing where there was no tape cuz we couldn't come in in the spring. So coaches Clark Hobby at the time I'm still under flow with the stuff that they were teaching with the little details of football cuz there was nothing else to coach on. So it was hey look, this is last year and we're going to just dive into this. So hey, this is what offenses do or this is the why behind what they're doing. Instead of it when you're coming kind of getting into it and just rolling through things um you're coaching the individual technique in this and how we want to do it but like we had none of that COVID year. So to be at home just you know on your laptop watching it and thankfully I was smart um able gifted enough where I was able to learn from a computer screen and not in person sometimes. So, really take that in and kind of understand how to see the game and how to see each player um on the field. It really helped I think uh move my career along the next step. >> And what about treating your body and and recovery and things like that? When did you get yourself a program? >> Clay >> That was like year >> Three-ish years ago, three or four years ago. Yeah. Um I had a program and it I liked it. Um but then Clay is coming in with the uh expertise, I'll say he has uh in that realm. Um has definitely uh definitely helped me kind of get to this point and feel as good as I do right now um and making that transition into the >> Was there a point at which you talked about what you learned watching tape with Zeke and Jordan and Kenneth Grant? Did Did you do it with them collectively at any point or has it been just different times and different ways? >> [laughter] >> It It's collectively through Clark I mean, Clark's amazing where um he It's It's an open room. So, when he's doing tape or watching film and we're all in there together and I see something or he talks about something or something that wasn't talked about. Hey, by the way, look at this backside. This is what we're seeing over here. So, that they can see that it's not just about the little things. There's a big picture going on out there, too. Um that's why I think football's the greatest game on turf is there's 11 guys out there. Um and all 11 have to be hitting on all cylinders to make a great play. Every play looks good on paper. Um so, uh I think to be able to do that last year and then yeah, then individually with these guys kind of asking questions as well as a group um in our own off time to sit down and kind of help them see the game as I see it and as Clark and the guys see it now half of these guys. >> Is there something you can point to in watching film in your past where you picked up a detail that really made a big difference? Like a guy tipping off if if it's a run or a pass or anything like that? >> Uh little things like that are tough um cuz guys are getting really good cuz now there's tape out there on themselves. And if you're good, you watch your own tape to try to make sure I'm not tipping anything, which guys do. Um so, it's tough to get a little individual detail off of one person or a one collective thing. Um and that's if you think you have it, the one time you do think you're going to take that shot and work off that, you're probably going to be wrong. Uh So, it it it's just a it's a collective a group of all I guess the whole big picture kind of what we talked about earlier of all of 11. Knowing everything from DND to play clock and all in between that, too. >> You guys faced Kirk Cousins uh last year in a different offense. What do you remember worked well in that game? >> Yeah, you know, it's just uh just getting pressure. Um and just, you know, helping throw things off their game and uh the timing of everything. Just to be able to get back there and just work our moves and hopefully uh make it a one-dimensional game. >> Similar question. Just what do you remember about facing Tyler Linderbaum Linderbaum uh last year? >> Uh quick. Uh and I mean, he reminds me a lot like Brewer in the speed aspect of things where uh very smart center. Uh going to be writing a lot of uh aspects and going to be quick and uh if you're wrong, he's a you'll know you're wrong. He'll he'll take advantage of that. So, we got to be on our A-game there. And uh excited for that challenge week one. >> So, Patrick, I'll ask you what I've asked everybody else. This is a season opener, but it's the start of a new era. So, is it a typical season opener or does it feel a little bigger than that? >> I think each game is bigger than the last one, if that makes any sense. But, no, we're definitely excited. Um it's a new regime. It's a new coaching staff. So, yeah, definitely excited to get after it with this group. >> What did it mean to you to find out you were named a team captain? >> I mean, it's it's the biggest honor. Um it's one of the things I had written up on my my board, my mirror that I see every day. And um uh definitely honored that my teammates see me in this light. >> What will it take for you to lead this team amid the youth movement? >> I think just you know, I think the biggest thing with going with this new group is just instilling the right things, leading by example, and setting the standard, especially at the offensive line position. Setting that standard and holding everybody accountable. I think that's the biggest thing. You know, like you said, very young team, so just building with this group and instilling the right thing so we can build a culture that can go a long way. >> I'm going to take the word consistency, put it off-limits for this answer, if that's okay. So, as you >> [clears throat] >> as you reviewed your season last year, what's the specific area that you thought you most wanted to improve in, beyond consistency? >> Uh I'd say the run game. I'd say just everything with the run game. Let's not use use the word consistent, but uh run game. Um and better with my hands, and I felt like especially during this camp, my run blocking was a lot better than last year, so yes. >> How was that improved? Is it just technique, or what what things did you do >> to improve that? >> I'd say technique, yeah, displacement, and um you know, the attitude's already there, and the mentality's there, so just correcting the aiming points and just technique of it all, and I think it's improved a lot. >> When you're up against an elite edge rusher like Max Crosby, what are the keys to remember? What what what do you want to do to him? >> I think with him, he's a dynamic player. Um So, with him, just beating him to a spot, getting your hands on him, um getting him off his game. He likes to play with a lot of swagger, so just, you know, getting him displaced off his game, getting him off his spots, putting your hands on him, being aggressive, and just getting him out of his game. I think once you get him out of his game, it's pretty much >> Does he compare to anybody that you face, I mean, I know you faced Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter, right? >> Yeah. >> I mean, you faced some some good guys. Does he compare to anybody for any reason? High motor or or any good against the run? >> He's a high motor player. I think his motor is um their defense runs off his motor, and he's a great player, so yeah, I'd say his motor. >> You get him off his game, does the trash talk fall into that, too? That aspect? >> I feel like yeah, he's a hothead, so um a lot of those things you could get in get in uh get into his game with that, but I mean, he's a great player, so you just got to stay on it all four quarters really with him. Yeah. >> Do you get the sense between now and kickoff that your buddy Kaden is going to want to be like left alone or talked to talked to a bunch? Like you see a guy that What do you think? >> With him, he's played at a really high level. You know, Bama is, you know, as close as it gets to it in college football, so he's been ready. You know, he's ready. He's Yeah. You don't got to tell him nothing. He's He's a different type of rookie, so he's ready. Yeah. >> What type of captain do you want to be for this team? And is there anything in particular from the previous 2 years that that caught your attention and maybe you thought, "I like that from that captain." >> Oh, okay. I had one I had two. You know, Terron Armstead learning from him my rookie year. I think he handled himself well around the building. He was a great leader, great captain. And then AB, he's another one in our room, so just learning from them, too, and yeah, taking notes and bits and pieces from them. Yeah. >> I was going to ask something similar. You said that you had that written on your board as something that you have a goal for this season. So, how do you approach this year with that goal in mind? Not to necessarily prove yourself to your teammates, but to show that's an honor that you're worthy of. >> I think every day if once you look at it every morning, you know, I wake up, brush my teeth, I see it, and I can envision myself, and it gets me going for the day. Reminders what you want to do. And every day you come into the building, you have that mindset, and you see your goals. I think it helps, so yeah. >> What were some of the other goals you have this season if you don't mind sharing? >> Okay. Um I got a lot, but uh All Pro, Pro Bowl, Super Bowl.

title: Coach Jeff Hafley meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: You guys are working on Labor Day? >> So are you. >> We're happy to be employed. >> [laughter] >> State of the art business. >> You know what the poison is? I forgot that it was Labor Day. That's basically every holiday is a show up >> Oh, we're so lucky to get Not Not quite. >> Perk gets the opener today. >> No, seriously? >> Oh, wow. >> Woah, hold on a second. >> He defers to the second half. >> I'm getting a conditional seventh round pick in 2020. >> Why are you Why are you doing this? You guys teaming up on me or something? >> He's not interested in captains, but he is. >> That's the short version. >> You [laughter] are. We announced the captains. >> Yes. >> Yeah. >> Thanks, Joe, for David Fraley was the last to talk about this. I guess. >> No, really. So, this half this is Monday of the regular season, obviously. Does this feel like a normal Monday regular season or is this something special being your position and the start of a different era? >> Um It It doesn't feel normal because we've had like an extra week. Usually Monday, you're kind of coming in and you're going over the previous game tape, and then you're rushing to start getting ready for the next opponent. Um you know, so nothing to do with me. This is about our team and getting them ready to play, but just have a little bit more time in a practice on a Monday, which we normally wouldn't do. So, it feels different in that regard, but besides that, it's just No, not not too different. >> All right, so I will ask about the captains then. What do you think of the group of six that that you have, and um did did all of them just feel like real natural leaders on this team? >> Um I'm excited. I mean, the players voted for those guys, and um I think they deserved it. In each of their own way, they've showed, you know, the ability to lead um in all different ways and I think it's I think it says a lot about those six guys that they received the votes from their peers and um you know, I'm excited for those guys. I think those guys kind of set the standard of what we want and what we're looking for, but it doesn't end there. I think, you know, developing leaders is very important and it doesn't have to just come from the captains and I talked to the team about that today. but I'm excited for those six guys. I think they've earned it and I think some of them a year or two ago or three years ago might not have been in that position, but you know, I think it's a misconception when you say, "Oh, you don't have any leaders here or there." I think you can develop leaders and there's certain ways to do that and it comes in many different ways. So, I'm excited about all six of them. >> With Malik specifically, how much do you like that it wasn't just that he's the quarterback, he gets to be a captain. He showed some real leadership moments I thought throughout camp. >> Yeah, and and I think that goes to anybody who's ever talked to him. You can feel that quiet leadership about him. He has a special way to connect with the players in his own way. Uh sometimes it's vocally, sometimes it's, you know, behind the scenes and I think a lot of it too is his work ethic and and the work he put in and, you know, if you if you think about it, I just think it's a really cool example of a guy who, you know, really started out rocky in his career, right? Didn't didn't really go very well, was traded to another team, was the backup and now here he is as a captain. So, I think it's a cool message for everybody who's on our team right now about, you know, being persistent, putting in hard work, being true to yourself and it doesn't always happen right away. So, I'm I'm really happy for Malik. >> What what role do the captains serve for you in terms of what your expectations are for them in terms of leadership? >> They're the stan- They are the standard. And that's what I'm going to talk to them about. I have talked to them about it, but like I said, it doesn't it doesn't end there. You know, leadership can come all throughout the team. They're just the guys right now that they need to set the standard. >> Coach, when Saturday gets here and you guys have gone through your walk last walk-through, what will you have need to have seen from the team in the week of preparation to know they're ready for Sunday? >> I think we're going to find that out on the opening kickoff. I mean, you know, that's when it gets real. you know, for me, the process is about putting in all the work. And that that's that's what it's always been for me. It's Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday. It's how hard did you work? How hard did you study? Did you Did you do the extra? Did you get with your coaches? And And then you go let it rip on Sunday. that's my philosophy. That's what I believe in. You just You have no regrets. If you do everything you possibly can do every single day, the best that you can, um learning from your mistakes in practice, going out the next day, getting better at them, just continuing to grind, putting the work, watch the tape, study the tape, and then Sunday, you just you go out there and you play free and fearless and and you see where it lands and you got you got to keep doing it again and again. Um but, you know, this group I'm excited for, but but we'll find out Sunday when we kick off. >> What are the kinds of things that you might want to um survey the captains about relative to pulse of the team, you know, practice intensity, travel decisions? What what do you thought think you might go to the captains for? >> There'll be a lot to go to them for. I mean, it it could be some of those things you just mentioned. Um it could be other topics, but there'll be constant conversation. I'm always talking to the guys and picking their brains, and I have always done that wherever I've coached. Um I want to know what they see, how they're feeling, and ultimately, I'm going to make the decision. I mean, that's just the way it's going to go, but I mean, there's certain things that I'm going to want to bounce ideas off of some of them. And it could be a variety of those topics. >> Do you hear about sort of a welcome to the NFL moment that rookies go through as well as well as some of the nerves that are associated with your first NFL game. So given all of that, what will your message be to the rookies and the way you'll be talking about it? >> Same thing I just talked about. Um it's why you work hard during the week. It's why you prepare. It's why if your process is right, you can go out and you can play free and there should be no hesitation in them knowing that I'll have their back and there is going to be some ups and downs. I mean, that's all these rookies. It's It's just how it's going to go. And you know, it's to me it's just how do you respond, you know, when something good or bad happens? What's the response going to be? And then there needs to be growth and you know, I'm excited to go on this journey with them. >> From a health standpoint, will Kazee, American, and Robinson are they the only two that you think are dealing with injuries now? >> They'll practice today. So we'll see how it progresses, but but everybody will be out there today. So I'm excited for that. >> How are you nerves-wise? What is it like for you ahead of your first coaching game, head coaching job? again, I just the way I just explained that process to you about the players is the way I'm going to approach this week. I'm going to study the game plan. I'm going to tweak the game plan. I'm going to go over the game plan until probably before kickoff and then go let it rip. Call the game on defense and make the decisions I need to make throughout the game, lean on the staff, and and make it make it not about me, about our players. But I'll be anxious for it, but I'll put in the work, so I'll make my calls fast and I'll be decisive and you know, you can't have any regrets on game day. You just got to go out there and coach free and do everything that you can and and respond. Um but I'll be more excited than anything else um to coach this team. >> You're unique in the cycle of coaches in terms of having head coaching experience previously among first-time NFL head coaches. How do you think that has benefited you most judging from your first five six months on the job here? >> Yeah, I think it's all benefited from me like just picking the staff for example. You know, I just I went through it. I had to hire a whole staff. I had to hire people. I had to let people go. I had to hire new people and I like I said, I made plenty mistakes in four years that again, you got to continue to learn. You got to continue to grow. Even being on the field, I mean, the first game that I ever coached on the field as a head coach, I was going over an adjustment with the defense and all of a sudden someone taps me on the shoulder and asked me if we want to punt. I'm like, "Holy cow, we're already got a punt?" Like so I've been through a lot of the moments. Um not that I'm not that I have all the answers and not that that there's not going to be a lot more that I have to learn from, but I've went through the games as a head coach and you know, did some things that I've, you know, made note of and and will do better the second go around. >> Coach, when you were in Green Bay, were you on the field or were you in the booth? >> I was in the booth. >> What are the kind of the the differences beyond maybe the obvious of calling a game from the field versus calling it from the booth? >> Yeah, just picture you're sitting up there in the booth. All my notes are laid out. Like everything and it's nice and quiet and all the emotions are kind of taken out of the game. So, it's just constant you're just working and in between series you're listening and you're taking notes and you're maybe scripting the next series and someone's handing you notes and you're studying the opponent's tendencies and all of a sudden you're studying this tendency and you're you know, maybe tweaking little thing here or there. You getting someone So, you're just it's like it's all slowed down. It's kind of like playing a video game up there. You can see it all. it's a lot different and um you know, I enjoyed obviously calling the game from there. It's just I got to be on the field now And I have Sean up there, and I think that is the equalizer cuz I his eyes up there is good as anybody that I've been around. The communication that we have, how he sees it, how I see it, we can kind of finish each other's sentences now being together for 8 years. Um so, he really he allows me to have the eyes that I need up there, and he'll be a big part of the defense and what we call, and he'll have plenty ideas. I mean, I have full trust in Sean. Um but I'm excited to be on the field. I I think with the young team that we have, being able to look them in the eye, being able to pick them up when they have a tough moment, being able to congratulate them, then sit them down and tell them they got to go do it again. I think it's really important for me to be around this team where you know, I I didn't feel that way or I would have been on the field in the last 2 years. >> On Sunday, you might get in your ear analytics say go, analytics say kick. how much of that do you think you'll go with analytics, and how much do you like to go gut feeling? >> Yeah, good question. I think during the week you study that, and you kind of have, you know, analytics say in in this game, in these situations, say for example, fourth and four on this yard line is a go. And then you say, uh let's tweak that. Let's probably go more fourth and two in that situation. So, I think what you do is we sit down, we have those conversations, and you kind of give them my mindset. So, then during the course of the game in this situation, it's hey, in this situation, we said fourth and two was a go. Right? And my gut at the time might be like, uh let's punt it. Or let's kick the field goal. So, I think you do your homework. I think you have a plan, and I think a lot of the times you try to stick with your plan, but there's always got to be the feel of the game, and where it's going, and the momentum of the game, and and how I think everything is going, and what the team needs from me right now. So, again, I have I lived through I lived through a lot of that. I think there was 1 year where I think we were third or fourth in in going for it on fourth down, and we were like 92% conversion. I felt our team needed it that year. And then there was another year where we weren't nearly up there. So, I think it's both. I respect the analytics, but there's also some things that's got to come down to the game. >> A lot of this the Raiders offense will go through Brock Bowers. Obviously, I don't want you to give away the game plan, but what goes into stopping an elite tight end versus stopping an elite receiver? >> Yeah, I just when he is an elite tight end, just watching the tape I have a ton of respect for him as a player. And he's totally shown he has the ability to change games, right? Um just depends how you use him. I mean, a tight end could all of a sudden wind up in the C area over here playing in the tight end position and then shift on the snap and be over here. They can line him up in the slot and then go one by three and put him on the backside of a nub. They can go three by one and put him all the way flexed out like an extra receiver. So, he gives them the ability to use them lining him up as a tight end and lining him up as a wide receiver. So, it kind of creates an extra variable than just say, "Hey, it's their extra receiver. I know he's going to be in the boundary in three by one or I know he's going to be the field in two by two." And then you can start game planning coverage for him based on which side he's on. This gives you another element where they can move him around even more. So, you just got to have You got to have a good plan because you better know where he is. Um and and and we'll have a bunch of adjustments for that. >> I'm not going to mention that. >> Building off of that, Max Crosby is an elite edge rusher, good against the run and the pass. Do you want your team like on edge and hyper aware of where he is or is it kind of a relaxed trust your training through the week? How how do you handle that? >> I think it's both, but you better know where he is. Um he's one of the elite defenders in the league that plays with a relentless motor. You can't just go into a game and say, "Hey, everybody take it nice and easy Max." No, you better know where he is, but then there's times when we're going to use our rules and play football, and then there's times when he's a guy that you better game plan around cuz he's another guy that can wreck a game, and we've all seen him do that. >> You guys open the season against a lot of quarterbacks who have played a lot of football, veteran guys. How do you want your young guys, especially on the defensive side, I know you have veterans on that side, but how do you want them approaching going against quarterbacks who have played a lot of football? >> I want them to play within the scheme, which is what I think they've done a really good job in camp, and trust their training. And, you know, the biggest thing when you get into these games early in the season is, you know, a lot of the calls that we've you know, that we have, they've been playing all training camp. Don't don't change who you are, and don't just all of a sudden try to make something up where, you know, you're going outside the framework of the defense, and all of a sudden there's a huge gap or a huge hole, and and we, you know, we're getting hit over the middle or we're getting hit down the field, and we have nobody there. Trust your training, do your job to the best that you can, and, you know, we'll continue to coach throughout the game and help them out. >> I'm not going to mention the Dolphins in terms of how I frame this question, but I am curious. Have you thought in general as a philosophy about whether you'll coach, whether you would coach any differently with a team that maybe doesn't have the best talent in the league, or be an underdog a lot in terms of being more daring, blitzing more, more trick plays, more bells and whistles? Have you had that thought in your mind over the over recent months, and and what's your thinking on that? >> I think every week it's going to be different. I think you go into every single game, and it's who you're playing, what are their strengths, what are your weaknesses, right? How are we going to attack what we feel are weaknesses? How are we going to protect against their strengths? And some games it might have to be more aggressive than others. I just I think that's a huge part of this league. A huge part of this league is match-ups, right? Everybody wants to always talk scheme this, scheme that. There's also an element of player versus player, and what can we do to maximize our player against the guy we believe is better and vice versa. So, it's all going to be based on that each week and I think that's the fun part of the game and coaching is every week is really a unique situation in a different season. >> How about special teams wise, it looked to me and I might be wrong that some of those waiver claims were special teams oriented. Is is that correct and and where are special teams right now as far as organization with all the personnel changes? >> Yeah, I don't I don't know if you know any of those claims were made just with special teams in mind. Um but I think anytime that you're you're looking to fill in your roster, you better have guys that can go out and help you on special teams. Um and and I think Sully's done a really good job with that. You know, time will tell. We've had not many real practices with them. So, I still we're still in the evaluation phase as we go through Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday to still see these guys really play football and then obviously in the early part of the season, but I think Sully and their staff have done a good job of filling in the roster with hopefully guys that will be able to help us on special teams. >> Thank you, Sheldon. All right, guys. Appreciate it.

There's no ownership to what they have. >> The old regime would have kept Keion Smith. The old regime would have kept Keion Smith. The old [clears throat] regime would have kept Charlie Heck. >> That was the old regime's project. That's not the same thing. >> I like that. >> They'll they'll get their own projects.
