title: Mike Vrabel on Preparing for Week 1 vs. Seattle | Patriots Press Conference
text: Morning. So, what do you got? >> Um we haven't seen Tre on all week at practice. Um do you anticipate him being able to play on Sunday? >> Well, we'll see how he feels today. We'll see if he can do anything. Um he's been working extremely hard to come back and uh you know, we'll see where where that goes here today. We we do have a few more days uh you know, before, but you know, we'll just see what he's able to do today. >> What is your level of concern, if any, with Christian Barmore um with him not practicing yesterday? >> Um I I think he'll be out there today. I think that um you know, this is something that we've I think if you followed last year, probably managed uh you know, throughout the season and you know, I respect how Christian prepares um when he's not out there and we try to give him exactly what he needs. >> [cough] >> Excuse me. [clears throat] >> Oh, sorry. >> Nope. >> Uh how has the week gone for you as what you've seen from your team so far? >> Good. Uh good. I mean, I thought uh you know, we need another good day today. You know, we still have time to prepare and and things to do and and focus on and and you know, what our jobs are and what our responsibilities need to be and um but I but I thought yesterday was was energetic. I thought that uh you know, guys were were were locked in and they you know, I do think that there's a transition to how we practice uh with shells on. You know what I mean? We talked about what the rules are and 14 padded practices, 13 now uh for the rest of the season. So, we have to be able to practice with shells on um and still be able to you know, practice with speed and and and do the things that we needed to get done, the timing of the plays and what we and how we need to react defensively. Um and so I think that's just a learning process. >> Regardless of Tre on's health, I imagine the level of faith in Ramondre is pretty high. >> Yeah, of course. I mean, it's it's high for for everybody that's here. Everybody here uh you You is asked and and they do prepare as a starter. You know, whether they get elevated or whether they have a limited role, they could be in there, you know, backup offensive lineman, a backup defense, you know what I mean? Whatever it may be. So, high high level of trust for for everybody that's here. >> When it comes to Amari though, what have you What have you seen from him this summer? Do you feel like steadiness, consistency? >> think that's probably a good way to put it. I think that there is a consistency. I think that um You know, we've talked about his his protection in the past and that'll be you know, critical, I'm sure, Wednesday night as it will be every night. And I think that's probably one of the the things I appreciate the most about him. Certainly love the the ability to catch the football and and and run with it and and create, you know, X plays, but also I think that the protection for for me is what stands out. >> Mike, just with the amount of energy that I'm assuming will be in the building on Wednesday, how important is it or how much time do you spend this week focusing on just having a good start? >> [sighs] >> Well, I think that um you you can focus on it and you can try to have a good start and we can say we have to get off to a good start. But then on the other hand, I would say, "Well, what do we do if we don't? Do we just leave? Do we just take our stuff and go home? Or or do we compete? Do we fight? Do we fight through adversity? Um So again, yes, it's going to be critical to to start fast and get off to a good start and all those things. But I I hope that we cuz at times throughout the season, we're going to need to be able to to fight through some things. There's going to be some things that we really don't want to have happen uh that happen. There's going to be a turnover. There's going to be an X play. There's going to be something. Um you know, look at Miami. We didn't want to Sure, we didn't want to give up a punt return. And we answered with a kickoff return. So, yes, we want to start fast. We always do. And but also, there's going to have to be some sort of response uh to our actions and and how do we keep our composure and and how do we come back and um you know, compete and and and find ways to win. >> Is there any way to know if your team can handle adversity? I mean, I know you had guys that were here last year and did and there were things that they went through, but new You're talking about new year. Can you put enough heat on them during the course of this summer? >> Well, we try, but I don't know if you ever really can replicate that. I mean, I think that we try. We try to make practice uh similar to the game as we possibly can. You know, we try to ratchet it up on them and and put them in those situations um whether that be in joint practices or the practices or the situations against our own defense or offense and and how they respond and get the ball down into the red zone or you know, going on the ball or all these different things that come up in a game uh that we hope that, you know, enough of those repeated actions uh is going to help us. But sometimes, you have to actually go through it and I experience it. >> On Hard Knocks, there was a segment where you were showing the team a clip about being firemen and living in the heat. Can you give some context to how you found that clip, why you showed it to the team, and the significance of that? >> Well, I just thought it was really cool uh you know, watching a you know, Hall of Fame trainer uh talk to the boxer and and say, "Hey, uh I can notice uh that you're wavering. Your concentration's wavering." And and the boxer, meanwhile, has never taken his eyes off the coach. And he's locked in. And he says, "I I need 15 minutes." And we play 15-minute quarters. And I just thought that there's going to be some times in the you know, we got one quarter left of the game that, you know, we're we're going to need to be able to lock in and focus and you know, there's nothing that that trainer uh the trainer's not going to be able to go out there, but he's going to be able to give him everything that he needs and the wisdom and the training to to help him do his job. And I felt like that was just a great relationship and a good connection between a coach and a player. on what we aspire to be. >> How big of a challenge is this for your offensive line and how much will you learn about this group just sort of out of the gate? >> Um well, every week's a big challenge. Certainly a huge challenge this week. I think that these very very talented, sound, play with great fundamentals. Uh they're good at with their games. You know, they have a very good mix of uh you know, youth and veteran players. And uh you know, Murphy, Leonard Williams, DeMarcus Lawrence, they've they they've all done it at a high level. And uh you know, whether they pressure or whether they game or they straight rush, uh they do a fantastic job of applying pressure. They're they're excellent in the run game. They play with their hands. They they play square. And uh you know, this will be a great challenge. >> I With um yesterday we spoke with Josh and when asked about getting Romeo and EJ, you know, ready to go, he highlighted Todd Downing and his job with those two guys. What have you seen from Todd and his ability to get that wide receiver room ready each and every week? >> Yeah, I think um Todd's done, you know, a really good job with you know, different personalities, right? Receiver Every receiver wants the ball. Every receiver wants 12 targets, 14 targets. And um you know, being able to teach them to to be in different spots and to learn what to do and and understand what their role is and how do they fit into what the quarterback's thinking. I've I've said this numerous times, but I I think that Todd's able to coach it from the perspective of a quarterback having coached quarterbacks uh and understand what it is with where they're starting in the progression. You know, are they front side, are they back side? Um and where they need to be, when they can play with patience, and you know, kind of hey, if it's man coverage, this is what the quarterback's going to need from you. He's going to need some sort of separation. He's going to need to trust that you're going to be inside if you're supposed to be inside leverage. Uh zone defense, this is what the quarterback needs to see. He needs to see spacing. He needs to see in between defenders and not, you know, plastered on one. So, you know, we're we're just getting started here, but you know, I think that Todd's, you know, got those guys ready to play. >> Okay. Okay. >> It's such a long lead-up to the game. Is there such thing as being over prepared? And I guess more so mentally for guys like, can you overthink >> Well, I mean, we're going to have to go out and play the game. We're going to have to go out and and they're going to We're going to kick the ball off. Um I think you can try to, you know, you start covering ghosts. And if this happens, what if this happens? Like, you know, there's a million plays and scenarios that could potentially uh come up in the game. And maybe some of them will, maybe some of them won't, but you know, I think just being able to have that right balance of, you know, are they Are they prepared? Do they know what to do? Do they have the ability to play uh with with speed and violence and play fast and aggressive, um but also not reckless and and making sure that we're communicating and that, you know, there's going to be things that we're going to see on Wednesday night that they maybe haven't shown or maybe we didn't show the guys because, you know, they only did it a few times. So, we try to show them everything that we can, but understand that there's, you know, some times out there where they're going to see some plays that maybe, you know, we weren't able to show them. And that happens every week, and you know, we'll we'll have to be prepared and be able to make adjustments. >> What goes into executing line games at a high level, and how important is the chemistry and communication when it comes to executing those assignments. >> Well, I think just the you know, the chemistry is critical about you know, who it is that you're working with and you know, somebody's got to get inside and somebody's got to be able to get vertical or somebody has to be able to sell that they're rushing and then they end up being the looper. So, you know, there's some there's some savvy to it and certainly there's there's a different style. Some some guys have a different style to it and uh you know, when you talk about Seattle, they they have you know, some guys will pass rush to to get into the gap and get vertical and you know, create a conflict with the you know, maybe say the guard and you know, but the communication is critical that they they're both on the same page. Is it a quick game? Is it a you know, delayed game? >> We talked to Jeremy yesterday about personal the job of personal punt protector. What do you look for specifically in that job? He had something really interesting. He said it's kind of like an offensive player because you have to block, you also have to run down. You focus on tackling. What are some of the unique things in that job? >> Well, that's everybody on the punt team except for the gunners, but I think that you need the communication skills of a of an inside linebacker or safety. You need the protection skills of a of a running back. You need the the mental you know, aptitude of a quarterback. You know, hey, this is where we're going to send the protection or this is what we want to do or the cadence. I have to be able to communicate and so it's it's a critical role. >> How do you think Handy kind of that first preseason game um he struggled. How have you seen him progress? >> that game. So, I don't remember what happened. Yeah. >> Um how have you seen him kind of progress throughout training camp? >> Well, I think the you know, like a pro. Like somebody that got back to work and you know, I think that they they have their own you know, the specialists have their own little world that they live in and you know, they I just ask them when they want to do the the kicking portion of of practice and then they go and warm up and they work on all their scenarios and the snaps and everything that they work with and I think he's been a consistent in his preparation whether that's the Mayday situation against Philly where we run in and we know in that situation you're not going to get a kicking ball you're going to get a regular ball he was able to make that so You know, we've seen a lot of situations in camp and and I've been impressed with with how he's performed. >> Like after watching him again this week preparing for him what's made what makes Jackson Smith-Njigba such an impressive player? >> Well, just the suddenness route craft you know, he's smooth he can play at different speeds he plays inside he run you know full full route tree you know, he's strong at the catch point but you know, I just think that the savviness and and the the ability to get in and out of breaks is is really impressive. Just want to have one update Caleb Lomax taken over for Will Campbell on the weekend update.

title: Zak Kuhr on season opener: "It's going to be a good challenge." | Patriots Press Conference
text: How would you describe the challenge ahead for your defense? >> Uh it's going to be a good challenge. Talented offense. You know, on the road, first game. >> [snorts] >> You know, a lot of guys didn't play in the preseason, so it's just some real live action. You know, we put an emphasis on working on the finish at practice. Put yourself in a good position to work the finish cuz a lot of you guys haven't done it yet, but it's going to be a good challenge. It will be. >> Zack, what do you make of their new offensive coordinator? I know obviously the scheme will stay similar, but what kind of research can you do on a guy who's never called plays at that level and put his own imprint on the offense? >> Yeah, you know, that's the challenge in that part that there's not you know, a a sample out there of what he's done in that regards, but you know, he comes from a a pretty strong offensive tree and like you said, you know, the last coordinator, similar tree, but you know, he's going to have his his thumb on it. You know, he's going to have his changes to it. And so really, we just got to make this game about us and you know, know our rules and our jobs cuz they're going to run something that we hadn't seen or practiced cuz we can't just go out there and guess on what it's going to be. Um but you know, they return a lot of guys, so we just got to have somewhat, you know, be familiar with what the old tree was and just play to our rules. >> Zack, I'm curious with uh the group of Christian, Farmer, Milton Williams, and Corey Durden. Um obviously Christian and Milton played together last season, but Corey's kind of stepping into that nose tackle role. How have you seen the three of them just grow and get better as like kind of a unit on the defense? >> Yeah, drastically [clears throat] better, I think since OTAs. Uh the chemistry's getting better with those guys, the communication, the things that they're saying, what they see on the field has gotten way better than what they did last year, but yeah, they're definitely growing together. You know, Clint and T and Abdullah, they're all doing a great job with those guys and they're developing and they know like all we have to do is just get better each and every day from up until game one, game one to game two, but yeah, they have they've drastically gotten better in that room >> How about Cory specifically? Obviously, [clears throat] he's kind of stepping into that role and you've talked about it all summer. What specifically have you seen from him and his kind of approach to that that position? >> Yeah, I've seen him embrace it and I've seen him you know, feel the [snorts] confidence with some success and hopefully it's a snowball effect in the positive way that one good play turns into two plays and three plays. I think you know, the more reps he's been getting during camp, the better uh his technique has gotten better and better and we're just working on consistency um and just his technique. >> Coach, you've had Jaylen Reed for a little while here. Just what have you seen from him and uh you know, how big a role do you think he could play in the defense? >> Yeah, I think there's uh some potential versatility there. I don't want to put that on him right now just cuz it's still new and you don't want to just give him multiple things at once. You still call him to hear even the little things of how we practice and how we call offensive terminology so we're all communicating the same way but uh I'm excited to work with J Reed. >> You guys lack some experience behind Tramon on the edge. Could Milton play on the edge for you guys or do you prefer to to keep him in the middle there? >> I would say everybody's available to do certain jobs if we need to. The one thing I think we take pride in what we do is you know, we always have a plan for whether it be injury or how the flow of the game is going and being able to adjust and if that's, you know, multiple people having to play multiple positions, you know, everybody stays ready for that. >> How do you feel about having to possibly rely on on Gabe and Quintavious just given the inexperience there? >> I mean when when you say rely, I mean I think they're doing a good job of learning the system, really honing in on just the the technique, the fundamentals, the details. And you know, like any rookie, like and there's going to be bumps and bruises and they're going to learn from it. We just can't have any error repeaters. Um but it'll be a good, you know, rotation. I think they'll have some good experience and learn from the experience. >> For you, how much unknown is there with the interior groups cuz you have I mean other than you know, Ponder, really just kind of a new group for you. >> Well, I wouldn't say unknown. I mean we had a lot of good practices in in the summer. You get to know those guys in the OTAs. So, I wouldn't say unknown. It would just be it'd be exciting to see how those guys go in game action, how they flow off each other and how the rotation works. >> I know Shane means a lot to Pylon. Means a lot to you just from the opportunity that he presented, I believe, with the Giants. Now that he's here, I'm curious how how's that fitting? You know, and what what does he say? >> Yeah. Yeah, and he's he's a sounding board. And, you know, if I have a question about something, I'll ask how he looks at it. Now, do we always agree? No. But, uh you know, he brings up great ideas. And it's, you know, more about does it fit who we have here? But, it's always good. I'm a big believer in I hear it from anybody. If if you know, the custodial staff has a good idea, I'll listen to it. You know what I mean? I think there's you can't just I I least I don't live in that world where I have this high ego and I think I have all the answer all that. I love hearing suggestions and ideas from everybody cuz all that can do is make us get a little more creative, uh bring more to the table that maybe somebody wasn't thinking about. It's a nice little think tank with him in there. >> And and is he doing the stuff like um not that [clears throat] it would be the same thing, but like Ben was doing like you know >> Some similar things, yeah. To McAdoo, yeah. Some similar things, yeah, he's helping with that. Yeah. >> The Christian is awesome. Curious given and that's kind of going on this summer. How have you seen him approach each day and can you just talk about the way that he's kind of been out there every single day of the summer? That he can be. >> Yeah, I mean Christian to me is the ultimate pro. I you know, he's handled his day just like it was last year. You know, he's a competitor. You know, he's obviously he's very talented. But he he's you know, he's a smart young man and uh he takes a lot of pride in his work. I know he doesn't talk much. But the way he goes about his business and how he prepares himself to me is I just I'm not speaking for him or anything. It's what I observe is unreal. It's unbelievable. It's it's calm, it's collected, it's methodical. Like like I said, I know he doesn't speak much but hopefully whenever he gets done playing that he's able to share with you know the next generation of football players of what his process is cuz he's got a great process. And he's been nothing but a professional. >> Do you think Do you think you'll have him out there on Wednesday? >> Uh anybody that's you know told to me that's available will be available. >> Zack, going back to the um three defensive tackle groups. We've seen some of that in nickel, some with base. What do you like about their ability to play more Christian and Milton on the edge and those groups maybe as a whole? >> Like what's the benefit to them being out there? Is that what you're asking? >> benefit of playing you know, you had one traditional edge and then three D tackles for stretches of team this summer. >> Yeah, I mean you know, there there's some give and take to that. Like sometimes you know, you get a little bit bigger on the edge and helps in the run game. Um but again, like just the versatility always helps showing different pictures of different people. So you're just not always static in the same spot. >> You had Darius with the Giants in 24. Shane had him last year. >> What type of player is he? >> Darius was my uh rookie in New York. Very excited to have him. Uh he's smart. He's a great teammate. He's a great person. He plays with violence. Um you know, he has versatility. >> [clears throat] >> And he just he goes about his business in the right way. I'm really excited to have Darius. >> With the Seahawks, um last year, you know, you were able to watch Kenneth Walker and try and prepare for him after that that Super Bowl game. This year they have Zach Charbonnet. Um how do you kind of prepare for that you know, how does the defense prepare for that run run running offense when you don't really know what to expect from a rookie? >> Again, you know, that's a great question. You know, you go off of what you see on film of what the expectation of what the Seahawks are trying to do in their run scheme. And you just have to do your best at you know, we've shown some clips from college and all that. We have to do your best to just try to put him into that system and what his running style is going to be. You know, you're not going to truly know until we get out there and you know, if adjust the way that he plays and see how what his playing style is, but same thing with a lot of unknowns. We just got to play to our technique, our rules, and adjust. >> Hey, going back to Shane for a minute. >> is there anything he did reflecting on last season the way you guys always break down once the season ends, you know, what you like? Was there any fresh insight given he wasn't here, but did he look back at anything you guys did last year and have some sort of perspective that you hadn't considered or heard? >> Yeah, I I you know, I would say in some areas, we had some conversation that he watched and said, "Hey, you know, I saw you did this. Maybe think about doing this. This could be better." Or "Hey, really liked what you do with this." "Hey, maybe you ever thought about tweaking this?" And those conversations stem from that. But yeah, he watched uh a decent amount of film when he first got here to have this conversation. >> Was that like big picture like how you know minute does that get technique versus personnel? >> Uh you know, I would Yeah, I would say it was a little more big picture than to to that. Yep. >> Thanks, Zach. >> Yeah, appreciate you guys. Thank you.

text: Afternoon. Well, morning. >> Uh just kind of a bonus practice, but still I'm sure it's encouraging to see Vea and Jaylen both work out there start the process of getting back. >> Yeah, it was. They got their first taste out there. So, we'll see how the week goes, but they ran around pretty good today. >> Didn't see Shaq out there. What is the latest on his status? >> Uh he's still rehabbing. He'll be a game time decision right now. >> What type of injury does he have? >> We'll disclose it on Wednesday. >> Todd, what's the off-season like preparing for the first handful of games? And how much time do you really chew on a game plan leading into this week one match-up? >> You don't chew much on it. You you watch everything. Obviously, different coaches move around a little bit. So, you kind of see different coordinators and everything. You watch everything and you go through the what ifs. Then you can watch too much film and it's not good for you. You got to get away from it. Then you got to get back to what can our guys do best and what we got to concentrate on to play fast and kind of that's what you go with. >> This team has always gotten off to really good starts under you. What what do you think the reason is for why this team has been so successful in week one? And then, you know, on the opposite side of that, I know the Bengals, they've actually struggled, you know, in their in their early season games. >> I don't think you can put too much stock in it. Every year is a different year. We just got off to a good start the past couple. And obviously, it means nothing going into this game on Sunday. So, we got to prepare like we need to prepare and play like we got to play. >> Your captains were announced. I I obviously, you've talked about the kind of the depth of leadership you have, but the idea that you can lose it like Evans and Lavonte David and still have the six you have, just it seems like it speaks to that. >> It does. It says a lot about them. I mean, Chris is not at all a drop-off from Mike. Obviously, Baker and Tristan are repeat captains. Uh Winfield and Vita as well. Antoine Winfield came in and he kind of etched his name in stone that way, but there was a lot of guys that got votes. I mean, it was it was probably closer than it has been in years. >> What What has Alex done since day one for him to earn the trust of so many people in this locker room so quickly? >> Well, he wanted the green dot, and he got that. And, you know, having a green dot requires you to talk and communicate with everybody. So, he's been done a great job communicating, especially with the safeties, him and Winfield and Ty Kee on the same page. Uh getting along with the defense and front lining everybody up, and then just making plays with his ability. Obviously, everybody has a lot of respect for him, and he kind of just played his game, and he worked his way into it. >> How does it help a player like Josiah Tratter he's in there next to Alex Anzalone as a Mike linebacker, not necessarily having to make those calls, but but just being able to line up and and play football? >> It allows him to play freely. Obviously, he can give him some tips in there as well on things that could and might happen the next play, but it allows him to play free. >> I know Jacob Harris is going to get a chance to play corner, and he's done that before. Um just what have you seen his development throughout this off season at that position, and what kind of a challenge is it to, you know, get these two receivers in week one? >> I mean, he's been outstanding in the off season. I think him and Winfield probably two of the guys that had the best off season that we can possibly have. Nothing phases him. He goes to work regardless of who he's going up against. He's going up against two of the best this Sunday. Obviously, they have some great receivers at hand, but he's just got to play his game and play proper leverage and make some plays, and I think he will. >> What's your assessment of Worsted? Because I know, obviously, he missed a lot of camp, but then we did get to see him in the third preseason game, and it appears he played really well. Just how would you assess where he's at, um just in general? >> I mean, I think he did a very good job coming back. He's healthy now. You've seen his speed all over the place. You can see him on special teams. You see him play on defense. Uh just getting the scheme down to where he doesn't have to think about it, and he's mostly there. He's still got a few ways to go, but he's mostly there. We like the way he's playing fast right now. He's just got to stay healthy. >> Like Jacob Parish, does that give you some different ways to go if you wanted to put Benjamin Morrison outside, you can move Parish to nickel, and if you wanted to get Ke'Shawn Scott in the field, Parish stays outside, and Scott can move into nickel? >> It does. It gives us a lot of flexibility. You know, everybody that's out on the field right now has played nickel at one time or another, so that gives us a lot of flexibility. >> Coach, we made it to game week. I'm sure you're excited. I know the team's excited. We're all excited in here. Um football's back. Why do you love football? >> Tell y'all that that Western Michigan Michigan game Saturday night, and football can give you a heart attack, so >> [laughter] >> I do love the game, and you like the heightening of it. I don't think I've ever been a part of one of those where I was standing down there, and they kind of stormed the field, and I kind of got caught up in that part of it, but, you know, it it's always exciting to start the season. Everybody prepares the right way. You're excited to see what you can do. You're excited to see your team out there. You're excited to see them execute, and, you know, it's different than the middle of the season or the end of the season, so there's a lot of excitement for everybody around. >> Just how special was it for you to be able to go to that game because in season you're typically not able to or or it's very difficult logistically. >> Any time I can get to see my son play is a great day. >> 12 tackles. >> Yes, he did. He had a good day. >> Todd, when you're coaching against the Bengals, and coaching against Joe Burrow on the defensive side, does that kind of challenge excite you for those type of things? Certainly not in a week-one matchup when you're going to go against those receivers as well. >> It gives you a headache more than anything preparing for guys like that. It's exciting once you get there, but, you know, those guys can give you a headache. They've given everybody headaches. >> What makes Burrow so special in your eyes? >> It's not just the accuracy. It's his intelligence, the way he moves in the pocket. He can run without running. He can buy time uh just sliding his feet. He can get 7 yd if he has to get seven. He can get 10 if he has to get 10. He can see the rush. Uh he's so accurate on the outside, especially with his fade balls, especially the back shoulder or the deep one over the top. And he puts it where only his guys can get it, and they do a great job going to get the ball. So, it's probably nothing he hasn't seen. So, we just got to try and play sound football and execute. >> Coach, across the league, Cincinnati has some continuity in offense, but there's 21 new offensive coordinators out of 32 this year. Early in the year, can that make it harder because you don't necessarily know tendencies or exactly what kind of offense you're going to go up against? >> I think it's harder for everybody early in the year. You haven't seen what tweaks the guys that stayed on are doing as well. So, nobody has a good feel until they get enough tape on you to realize what you're doing. >> We just talked to Yaya yesterday. How much has he grown, you know, as a leader? He's obviously got a young guy on the other side. What have you seen that relationship blossom in the offseason? >> I think he's really grown and getting the scheme down and understanding what he has to do and how to play. But, in doing so, understanding the defense and then talking to the other guys, knowing that the pass rush has to work together, and it's not just him out on the edge trying to get a sack right there. And him and Baine talking to each other as well as him and Canty and Vita and setting each other up. And that part of his game has really grown. >> Coach, when it comes to Takitaki Smith, how has he progressed as maybe like a either a deep third or like center fielder in terms of his deeper coverage? >> He's very smart. He's always been good back deep. He can play anywhere, you know, he can play anywhere cuz he sees everything. He's just one of them guys that you can count on, and you can go down an alley with, and you know he's going to be right there battling it out with you. But, he's a very intelligent player. He's a tough player, and there's not a lot of ball he hasn't seen. So, we trust him completely. >> Okay. Thank you. Yeah.

So, you kind of see different coordinators and everything. You watch everything and you go through the whatifs and you can watch too much film and it's not good for you. You got to get away from it and you got to get back to what can our guys do best and what we got to concentrate on to play fast and kind of that's what you go with. >> This team has always gotten off to really good starts under you. What what do you think the reason is for why this team has been so successful in week one? And then, you know, on the opposite side of that, I know the Bengals, they've actually struggled, you know, in their in their early season games. >> I don't think you can put too much stock in it. Every year is a different year. We just got off to a good start the past couple and obviously it means nothing going into this game on Sunday. So, we got to prepare like we need to prepare and play like we got to play. >> Time your captains were announced. Obviously, you've talked about the kind of the depth of leadership you have, but idea that you can lose Mike Evans and Levante David and still have the six you have just it seems like it speaks to that. >> It does. It says a lot about him. I mean Chris is not at all a drop off from Mike. Obviously Baker and Tristan our repeat captains uh Winfield and Vita as well. Analone came in. He kind of etched his name in stone that way but it was a lot of guys that got votes. I mean it was it was probably closer than it has been in years. What what has Alex done since day one for him to earn the trust of so many people in this locker room so quickly? >> Well, he wanted the green dot and he got that. And you know, having a green dot requires you to talk and communicate with everybody. So, he's been done a great job communicating, especially with the safeties. Him and Winfield and Tai are on the same page. Uh getting along with the defense up front and lining everybody up and then just making plays with his ability. Obviously, everybody has a lot of respect for him and he kind of just played his game and he worked his way into it. >> How does that help a player like Josiah Troder if he's in there next to Alexandone as a mic linebacker, not necessarily having to make those calls, but but just being able to line up and and play football. >> It allows him to play freely. Obviously, you can give him some tips in there as well on things that could and might happen the next play, but it allows him to play free. I know Jacob Parish is going to get a chance to play corner and he's done that before. Um just what have you seen his development throughout this off season at that position and what kind of a challenge is it to you know get these two receivers in week one? >> I mean he's been outstanding in the off seasonason. I think him and Winfield probably two of the guys that had the best off season that we could possibly have. Nothing phases him. He goes to work regardless of who he's going up against. He's going up against two of the best this Sunday. Obviously, they have some great receivers at hand, but he's just got to play his game and play proper leverage and make some plays, and I think he will. >> What's your assessment of Morrison? Because I know obviously he missed a lot of camp, but then we did get to see him in the third preseason game, and it appears he played really well. Just how would you assess where he's at? Um, just in general, >> I think he did a very good job coming back. He's healthy now. You're seeing his speed all over the place. You can see him on special teams. You see him play on defense. uh just getting the scheme down to where he doesn't have to think about it and he's mostly there. He's still got a few ways to go, but he's mostly there. We like the way he's playing fast right now. He's just got to stay healthy. >> Like Jacob Paris, does that give you some different ways to go? If you wanted to put Benjamin Morrison outside, you can move Paris to nickel. And if you wanted to get Kee Scott in the field, Paris stays outside and Scott can move into nickel. >> It does. It gives us a lot of flexibility. You know, everybody that's out on the field right now has played nickel at one time or another. So that gives us a lot of flexibility. >> Coach, we made it to game week. I'm sure you're excited. I know the team's excited. We're all excited in here. Um, football's back. Why do you love football? >> Tell you, I was at that Western Michigan Michigan game Saturday night. And football can give you a heart attack. So, [laughter] I do love the game. And you like the heightening of it. I don't think I've ever been a part of one of those where I was standing down there and they kind of stormed the field and I kind of got caught up in that part of it. But, you know, it's it's always exciting to start the season. Everybody prepares the right way. You're excited to see what you can do. You're excited to see your team out there. You're excited to see them execute and you know, it's different than the middle of the season or the end of the season. So, there's a lot of excitement for everybody around. Just how special was it for you to be able to go to that game because in season you're typically not able to or it's very difficult logistically. >> Anytime I can get to see my son play is a great day. >> 12 tackles. >> Yes, he did. He had a good day. >> Todd, when you're coaching against the Bengals and you're coached against Joe Burrow on the defensive side, does that kind of challenge excite you for those type of things? Certainly not in a week one match up when you're going to go against those receivers as well. gives you a headache more than anything preparing for guys like that. It's exciting once you get there, but you know those guys can give you a headache. They've given everybody headaches. >> What makes Brow so special in your eyes? >> It's not just the accuracy, his intelligence, the way he moves in the pocket. He can run without running. He can buy time uh just sliding his feet. He can get seven yards if he has to get seven. He can get 10 if he has to get 10. He can see the rush. Uh he's so accurate on the outside, especially with his fade balls, especially the back shoulder or the deep one over the top and he puts it where only his guys can get it and they do a great job going to get the ball. So, it's probably nothing he hasn't seen. So, we just got to try and play sound football and execute. >> Carson, Cincinnati has some continuity on offense, but there's 21 new offensive coordinators out of 32 this year early in the year. Can that make it harder because you don't necessarily know tendencies or or exactly what kind of off to go up against something. >> I think it's harder for everybody early in the year. You hadn't seen what tweaks the guys that stayed on are doing as well. So, nobody has a good feel until they get enough tape on you to realize what you're doing. >> Let's talk to I guess how much has he grown, you know, as a leader? He's obviously got a young guy on the other side. What have you seen that relationship blossom in the offse? I think he's really grown and getting the scheme down and understanding what he has to do and how to play, but in doing so, understanding the defense and then talking to the other guys, knowing that the pass rush has to work together and it's not just him out on the edge trying to get a sack right there and him and Bane talking to each other as well as him and Ky and Vita and setting each other up and that part of his game has really grown. >> When it comes to Tea Smith, how has he progressed as maybe like a either a deep third or like center fielder in terms of his deeper coverage. >> He's very smart. He's always been good back deep. He can play anywhere. You know, he can play anywhere because he sees everything. He's just one of them guys that you can count on and you can go down an alley with and you know he's going to be right there battling it out with you. But he's a very intelligent player. He's a tough player and there's not a lot of ball he hasn't seen. So, we trust him completely.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Gives Final Updates Ahead Of Week 1 | Seattle Seahawks
text: Got a game pretty soon or what? Good to see everybody. Uh Some fun rules at the beginning of the season. This is great. This is a fun week. I get to I get to not answer anything. So. You can try if you want. >> Mike, how's Nick Bosa working? >> [laughter] >> Uh Nick Nick had the his probably most work in the in the last couple days. Looks great. And he practiced limited today. >> Ty Ivi Ty Davis or anything you can say on Ty or >> Uh yeah. Ty Ty Ty didn't practice today. >> What kind of an off season [laughter] did Rodney Thomas have? And what do you like his readiness is to step in if that's the direction you're going? >> Uh Rodney had a great off season. We're really excited to be able to acquire him in the off season. Uh has a lot of range, ball skills. Uh physicality. I thought he played really well in the in the games when he was out there and he's practiced great. Um really like everybody everybody that's practiced with us and been here throughout camp. Um would be excited to see him, you know, just excited where they're at and we feel like they could contribute to us playing great football for us. >> What's what's the Anthony Bell's greatest trait going back to you guys? >> Uh physicality. Yeah, for sure. Physicality. Um D Bell's also another one of those guys that's done a great job since since he's been here. I know his journey's a little a little different and a little different than Rodney's, but again, this you know, 70 man roster and he's he's part of the 70, so we're excited about that. >> Mike, if Nick Bosa doesn't [snorts] play in the game this week, what does that mean? >> Um Yeah, Ty didn't uh Ty didn't practice >> Mike, what have you seen from the guys at practice going into the first game of the season? Just >> Yeah, we've I thought we've had really really great practices. did some really did some good things today. I thought our intent was right. I think understanding how we want to practice on a Friday. It's Friday today. How we want to practice on a Friday with a lot of the guys that haven't been here. Just being aligned in terms of the speed. It's a combination of like a it's not as not as crazy of a practice that we're looking for, but we're looking for high-powered execution at the same time. So, we're still kind of connecting those dots to a certain extent, which is okay. Um but I think I think the guys understand like the week's not over, you know, we're we still have um opportunity to really nail some of these details that we want to get to uh going into the going into the game. So, um but very pleased with our intent, our attention to detail, but we're still not we're still not there yet. We got some things that some eyes to dot and tees to cross, I think, before uh before the game. >> We Emmanuel also be someone who's had a really good in the spring managing to limit and then you get a little bit after that. But what what have you just kind of his campus >> Yeah, I think I think we saw the same things you did, Bob. Just uh he's he's um things taken off, things have opened up, things kind of come out of his shell a bit since he got here. Understanding how we uh how we operate. And uh you know, since since he started practicing again, he's put himself in a great position. So, he's doing a great job. >> With obviously he's still a few games away before he's allowed to play. How is Zach kind of developing and how is he going to play in the first game of the season? >> Yeah, it's a whole process. Zach's doing awesome. Doing awesome. I think he has a certain timetable in his mind that uh which we won't divulge right now, but like he has a certain timetable that uh he he's targeting and he's on target for that for for timetable, which is great. It's an aggressive timetable from if you just kind of put the whole thing into perspective. I think that shows uh what type of guy he is, you know, just being able to come back and work through that process and, you know, get over those hurdles that it takes to put himself in this position, but I mean, he looks awesome. He looks awesome going through go uh whenever I see him doing anything, he looks looks pretty damn good. Yeah, it's it's business as usual. And I really that's that's the uh that's really our directive to our team is the way we want to train, the way we want to play games. There's a lot of There's a lot of circumstance that comes around with this game as did our last game, but our focus has to stay uh on who we are and how we play ball, you know, if we start getting affected by all the things around it. Uh you know, you're not going to we're not going to be the best football team we can be. And And he's right there, you know, in terms of having the the right type of attitude on how to on the approach, so uh I feel like he's in a really good good place and uh again, I'm I'm just I'm excited to see him play. >> You've talked uh not about the injured guys that much, but uh for the guys that you do have, having Tyrese Knight step forward, being able to go to five-man lines and the 10 and the edges that you've got, uh what are you looking forward to seeing from some of those guys that can step in and take some of those those reps? >> Well, I I would say that we have a lot of guys that have earned opportunities to play and we spent a lot of the offseason getting them ready to play. So, whoever's ready to play is going to we have a lot of faith in playing good football for us, so however we deploy them, you know, again, we're we're we're we're two different football teams right now, so like for us to dust off the last game plan and and just say that's what we're going to run is is overly irresponsible, nor is it the best thing for this team, so um we have a game plan that what's we're going to try to execute it to the best of our ability and it's and as coaches we have to do a great job of uh understanding how the game's being played and be able to adjust uh more so probably than any other game in the season because of just being week one and you know, both teams are kind of you know, they haven't really they haven't had to show their cards yet. >> Christian Haynes is in his third year with you now. What do you kind of think of his camp and how he's progressed since after getting a couple of games under his belt last year and where he's at this year? >> Yeah, we've had we've had really good competition um at the guard position. And there's a there's several guys on our team that uh have done a great job and Christian's one of them. I think he's really taken his game to another level, so um he should be proud of himself. He's done a he's done a really nice job. >> Coach, are you prepared to work with Adam Dearth for the third season? Could you discuss the qualities of your British defensive coordinator? >> Can I discuss the what? >> The qualities. >> to miss one at least one question at least one word. I'd love to, yeah. AD he's a he's a corner cornerstone piece of our of our club, you know, he's um he's been there every step of the way since since day one. he's a heck of a football coach. He really is. How he sees the game I think compliments how I see it in terms of how we've how we've built our team and built our you know, scheme. his probably his best quality is just being a connector and a leader and communicator. There's three, not just one. But uh we love him. He's a he's done a tremendous job. And uh we trust him, you know, he's he's he's running the operation 99% of the time. And uh one of the cool things about AD is like I think if you came into our defensive team team room, I don't I don't know if you'd be able to figure out who the coordinator is or who the DB coach is or who the head coach is. It's just kind of everybody pulling in the same direction and he definitely sets the tone for for that feeling and that's what we're trying to create. So, uh can't say enough good things about him. >> Mike, since the Dallas preseason game, where have you guys grown operationally in things you want to do between the snaps? >> Yeah, the the guys have been on it. They've done a really nice job. Uh coaches, players included. Sam's really driving the bus on that front. Uh offensive line's bought in. They see it. I'm I'm excited to see him do his thing. >> How's How's Brian Flores grown in that regard just in the month? >> Well, he has a clear vision on on what he expects and and uh and he communicates in his way, which is effective. And I, you know, any anytime anytime you put anytime we kind of see something that we want to improve on, and we kind of put our intention behind it, you want to see you want to see growth, you know, from really everybody involved. And and Brian really helped push that offensively, and so I appreciate the way he went about it. >> You guys have a lot of continuity with the coaching staff and with the players. Where do you feel that helps the most in in terms of the menu you can call, the time that it gets takes to get a game plan in? Where do you see the difference? >> I don't know how much quicker it's got on defense. Uh I do I do think I do think we understand um the things that we want to get to sooner. It's a just it's just a shared understanding about how we do all the things. Like do what schematics we want to get to, what answers do we feel like we wanted to maybe we find something that we need to be able to fix, how we can get that coached. There's just there was a cool moment the other day where we were in special teams, and I told our staff this, but I just felt like it's probably this is probably a good time to share it, but it's like during special teams period, the guys, you know, we have we have a operating procedure on who needs to be out there and when and all that type of stuff at the beginning of practice, but like our entire defensive staff, I think might have been working with another part like another position a different position group than they normally work with and so it's just this really cool uh synergistic 12 as one type of idea of hey we coach everybody all the time. there's no again there's no such thing as like we only farm each other's land you know it's it's a team effort and uh just a great attitude and and the player you know the favorite players are getting developed and they're learning stuff and it's just just uh it was a really cool moment that I was just like man this is this is awesome. >> How important is it to you to have coaches with like cross discipline stuff like you could have a tight end coach be a tight end coach for 30 years as opposed to somebody who >> No not that important really just a spirit of how you go like you just got to just got to be one of us man you got to can't just operate in a silo you know don't just close your door and worry about your guys that that doesn't that doesn't go over here pretty well. >> You mentioned that there's sort of an un- an unknown element in the opener where teams haven't shown their cards and there's uniqueness to that so how do you prepare yourself to be able to overcome the unknown element where the opener is a little bit different than maybe than week two or three or four? >> Well you I think you have to stick to your core competencies at the beginning of the game and then you know you you're you're going to build out some possible answers as it goes but it's just a really having an understanding of what you can do who you guys are how you feel like what they're trying to do and then then get to it I you're doing that every game anyways but I think the first game it's it's just uh it is different just probably cuz it's you know they could do anything you know you just got to be ready for it. >> What are you looking forward to most about this season? >> I haven't really thought about I mean it's Friday right now. Right now I'm thinking about the things I'm doing right after this and then uh working on a little red zone and and then getting home. >> Is there anything built into the schedule that the new owners get in front of the team at any point to introduce themselves? >> It's up to them. It's up to them. They're the boss. >> Anything else? >> Okay. >> Thank you.

title: Brian Fleury: "We're Going To Just Play Seahawks Football" | Seattle Seahawks
text: All right. Hi. How we doing? >> How's it going? >> Great. Anybody want to start? I don't have any opening remarks. >> How uh you get your first chance to call plays in an NFL game and all that? How uh how much are you looking forward to that? >> Uh obviously I'm really looking forward to it. I've had more fun out here at practice these last 2 days than probably any of the last 7 years, so I'm excited to continue this journey and and get out there for the first time on Thursday. >> What's been fun? >> Uh just going into the game plan process with the guys and uh you know, it's such a great group of guys and they have so much experience together. They all have great ownership of the offense and so, you know, being able to talk about things and how I see it and how they see it and make sure that it's all uh synchronized together has been really fun. >> I'm wondering if anyone Brandon if you sought for advice on this whole experience. >> Unfortunately, the people I would seek advice from aren't really interested in seeing us do well, so not not many. >> What have you seen this is obviously your first camp working with Sam or about it? What have you seen that in him? >> It's my second camp working with Sam, but uh >> First as the coordinator I should say, sorry. >> Yeah, I mean just his his growth over the last 3 years since I've been with him and his confidence level has increased significantly and his ownership of the offense and his his command over like just the room and the group has really been really impressive. >> Are you feeling like >> guys today that communication is super important week one when you're adjusting on the fly. When did you know you were over the hump and making sure that messaging was clear across all phases? >> Uh messaging has been clear since I walked in and that's a credit to Mike and John. Um we really kind of got over the hump as we got back into training camp. I think it became really clear. We you know, had some growth opportunities in the off season as they were getting used to how I see things and you know, they were coming from Clint's uh offense and and how they saw things and then when we got here in training camp is really when we kind of hit the ground running within that first week. >> Used to be in the '80s that speed was about vertical stretch. Um now you see it used for stretching field horizontally as well. Talk about how those two things work together. >> Yeah, obviously you want mixed elements. There's vertical separation which you can create with speed down the field, but also, you know, horizontal could be lateral quickness. This like the shorter area moves similar to like a Wes Welker or something like that. Um, and then there's also the ability just to use the entire width of the field with the same type of speed that you would stretch it vertically with. So, you know, if you're using all 54 53 and a quarter yards and whatever's left to the end zone, you're doing a great job. >> Are you Are you going to be down on the on the field or up in the >> Yeah, I'm going to call it from down. I was really pleased with the communication from upstairs. Justin Outten's doing a great job. Tyson Prince is up there, too. And the the information and the um, and Daniel Stern, also, the the quickness with which they're getting it to me has been outstanding. So, I feel very comfortable being on the field. >> What are the pluses to doing it there? >> Uh, I just like being able to communicate in real time with the players. Um, you know, the way I want to call the game last about two series and then you get into the flow of it. There's adjustments being made and it gives me an opportunity to preview maybe things on the call sheet that I want to go to next and why. Um, and anticipate just like one little nugget of coaching point that I think might make a difference. It's just easier to communicate that in person face-to-face when you're dealing in like microseconds. You know, I I just like that part of it better. >> You remind us two series? >> What's that? >> What do you mean the way you want to call a game only last two >> I just mean, I mean, we're we're dealing with outdated information in terms of what the New England defense is going to look like. And so, how they decide to play us will start to take shape within the first two series is what I mean. >> Can you remind us which preseason games you did it from the field? >> Uh, I was on the field the first one against Dallas and the third one against Kansas City. >> Coach McDaniels, you came in here with the staff not working with you whereas you're working with the staff that are here. So, what's that collaborative process been like? Have you come up with your ideas and they have a lot of stuff from last >> Yeah, I mean, it we've all grown in that regard, you know, like I've obviously this is a great coaching staff. They just come off winning the Super Bowl. There's a lot of great coaches. One of which I had the opportunity to work with before, but in a different role. And so, we kind of had to go through a process of our own of them learning exactly how I see things and how I want to call the game. And that was a lot of like me being the voice and them listening. And then once we got to a point where they felt comfortable with that, it's been easier for me to turn things over to them cuz they can kind of see it through the lens that I would see it. And so, that's been the really fun part of these three preseason games and now going into this game is now kind of handing things back over to them and seeing what they can bring to me from a collaborative standpoint. It's been really cool. >> You were on the other side of the sideline for the first game last year in the win field. And And that was a game that kind of was different than all the other offensive games. They only wanted to play action pass. And so, the Seahawks offense kind of changed identities a little bit in that game. How do you approach this game to make sure you call your game and maybe not, you know, fall to adjusting to your opponent too much? >> Yeah, I mean there's always an adjustment to the opponent, right? You want to take away their ability to do what they want to do well. Um but I think that fits well within what we want to do. Uh we're just going to play Seahawks football. And that's, you know, what Mike has always said. We're going to be fast and aggressive and you know, just try and control the game and put pressure on the opponent any way we can. >> Cooper Kupp was telling us about the call it periods in practice. How important you feel like those have been for you and just getting ready to do it? >> Those have been great. Um it great for me, but also great for us as a unit for them to kind of hear in real time the way I would like to sequence things and how one play can lead into the next and the next and the next. Uh and just kind of feel the flow of it. >> Given the background with your your your stepfather obviously the and it sounded like you kind of were thinking coaching maybe at a pretty early age. >> Yeah, at a pretty early age. It uh I wasn't a very good football player after high school. And so, as soon as I realized that that was the only way I was going to be able to stay involved, uh that's kind of the direction I went. >> Did you always think something like this was was realistic for you or was there when did that >> Uh I No, I didn't think that grandly. Uh I mean I as a kid I always wanted to be a part of the National Football League, so you know, that part of it has always been there. I've always had a lot of respect and admiration for the people that play football in this league and the people that have like helped build it from the ground up, but it was really more about the teaching for me early on, just like taking what I knew from a knowledge standpoint and just being able to help people get better. >> And I heard you I'm sorry, I heard you describe yourself once as kind of a non-athletic quarterback, is that right? Or >> Yeah, I'm I I played a different brand of football than Jalen likes to play out there, if that's >> Given that the guys you're playing with on Wednesday haven't seen time during the preseason, are you kind of curious about how that communication's going to actually go when those guys are in the fire and how that's all going to work when you're going with the guys you got or did you get enough >> No, we got enough work. I'm not I'm not concerned about the communication at all. We've done enough simulations here where I feel good about that. I'm just excited to go out there and watch them execute. >> This is your first time actually being in the ear of the quarterback before the the mic gets turned off. How has that communication been and what what do you try to communicate during those >> Uh we try to communicate beforehand. It's I mean, you've seen some clips, right? They they don't like to hear too much information and the sequencing is important. Like if I want to give them a reminder, it has to happen before I call the play, cuz if I try to call the play and then tell them something else, then they get something lost. So, you know, that part of it is important and I had to learn that and Sam's been great about giving me feedback from that and I think we're going to be rolling rolling just fine. >> Are you a wristband system or do you like to call it? >> It's a mixture of both. We'll have some stuff on the wristband that is like maybe a little bit more verbose or game plan specific, but anything that's something that we've been using from a terminology standpoint since we got here and into training camp that they're comfortable just hearing and saying, then we just roll with that. >> Your rookie tailback, which you work with him every day, but he hasn't played since November. What are you curious about Wednesday night? >> I'm just excited. I wouldn't say curious. I'm just excited to watch him play. I'm excited to see him get his first touch. I'm excited to see him be able to play in this atmosphere and uh I think it's going to be the beginning of a a really good career. >> Some of your players have described you as pretty even-keeled, stoic, uh reserved. Where do you think that kind of comes from and do you agree with those assessments? yeah, I would agree with their assessment. Um you know, what's portrayed on the surface isn't really what's going on internally. So, I would agree with that for the most part. Usually when something good happens, I'm thinking on to the next scenario and I'll celebrate at the end. You know, that's kind of my personality. >> Were you taught those lessons or was that kind of organically? >> No, it's just organically kind of how I've always been. >> Were you on the field coaching for San Francisco previously? And do you like being on the field as opposed to being in the >> Yeah, there's advantages to both. I was on the field for the last 4 years in San Francisco and upstairs for the first three and then upstairs everywhere else I was around the league. So, I've had a lot of experience of both. Again, the communication part with the player, like if you're if you're trying to communicate directly with the player, there's something about picking up the phone that like just doesn't vibe best for me. So, I like to be able to have the face-to-face eye contact conversation with those guys whenever possible. >> Mike has talked about that he sometimes could be drawing things up and making adjustments the night before and implementing those in the game. What's your style? How quickly do you kind of lock things down? >> Yeah, I I try not to make too many schematic changes. There There was definitely a couple times in the preseason where I would add a play, but that again, like if I'm going to add a play, it's something that we're all comfortable with and I can go position to position and say, "Hey, I think I'm going to call this on the next drive. Is everybody good?" Um the the the way the game is going to be called can evolve right up until kickoff as you're thinking of matchups and situations and then again, as you see how the defense is coming out and playing you. So, like there's an element of the game plan that shifts over, you know, the course of time, but not like just adding random stuff. >> What do you think with Elijah's preseason? Seemed to have a pretty good What what do you kind of see about him and what are you excited about this >> Uh I saw a lot of growth from what I saw on film last year. Um he still has a lot of room for growth and I'm excited. Hopefully he can put around some consistent playing time here early on and just continue to trend in the right direction. He'll definitely be out there. We've got some things that we're going to use him with for on the you know that'll be fun to see. >> How have you seen Sam take to the stuff that you're bringing? Obviously it sounds like it's going to be a very similar offense to last year, but the stuff that you're bringing with you, how have you seen him take to that? >> Uh he's taking to it great. Uh we've you know, it's just ongoing dialogue. There's there's things that he loves and things he maybe doesn't love so much that we can come to an agreement. Maybe we do want to try and push forward and get better at this or some things that we've just said, you know what this isn't worth the investment. So uh I mean he seems very comfortable overall with kind of where we've landed in terms of this game. >> The Rams ran a lot of 13 last year. You of course coach tight ends. What are some of the pros and cons from being able to to get heavy like that in terms of whether they're going to match or they're going to play nickel? >> Yeah, so that's a really interesting conversation because last year I think they caught a lot of people off guard by doing that especially in those first few weeks. And so when you get into bigger groupings usually it simplifies the defensive menu. But as they continue to put it on the field the defensive menu continues to grow as people become more and more prepared. So going into this season while that might seem like an advantage trends for an offense to do the entire league has had the entire off-season to come up with their plan for defending 13 personnel. So I don't think you're going to see quite the same advantages. We will have some of it available and you know deploy it when we feel appropriate, but I don't know that you're going to get quite the level of production that the Rams had out of it just league wide. >> Anything else? Thank you. >> Okay. >> Thank you. >> Yeah.
