text: This is the OTP. It's time for the regular season. I'm Taylor Zarzer and we're joined by the head coach of your Tennessee Titans, Robert Salah. We're excited to be with you as it's game week now, coach, in the National Football League. And I know that's music to your ears. >> Oh, yeah. Fun starts now, right? >> Yeah, it does. uh 229 days, coach, from the time you and I sat in these chairs, by the way, in a different room. And you were announced as the head coach of the Tennessee Titans. That's a long time, but I know that you've been working on this day with your team and your entire organization. >> Uh you know, we have been and and time flies. It feels like yesterday to be honest with you. Um but uh but a lot of work has been done. A lot of work still needs to be done, but uh we're excited to get this thing going. you've been so intentional uh with your team and with everyone in the organization about what the offseason program would look like and then you made it very clear in this room to us that there would be a new message when training camp would start. Is there a shift again coach as the regular season gets underway? You know, it's uh not not really. And it's because at the end of the day, you know, we we've been talking about process and now we're in a position where we're going to be judged for our results. And you can't let that interfere with what we've started, which is being great processoriented uh individuals and and doing everything we can to be the best we can be and uh and chasing process more than result. The the the result's going to be the result's going to be the result because of great process. And um and so we just got to maintain keep the main thing the main thing control the things that we've got control over. Uh put our best put our pos put ourselves in position to put our best foot forward and whatever happens on Sunday happens. >> Seems like an example of what you're saying is be present. We're going to attack it today. We're not going to think about what's happening weeks from now. We're going to be in charge of dominating this practice and this workout routine, etc. >> Yeah, it's uh it goes back to what we said. Um, I think I've said it a million times. Go to bed better than when you woke up. >> And if you keep that main focus, uh, attack every moment of every day, whether you're making your bread bed, brushing your teeth, it doesn't matter. Uh, be the best you can be in that moment. And, um, odds are you you'll love the result. >> You had to finalize the roster, coach, from, uh, training camp to the regular season, and I know that's something that's always really difficult to do in the National Football League as you trim down that roster. Tell us how that process went. Uh it it's difficult every year, you know, like um of the guys that are are cut from the roster. There there's conversations you're having that you just you just know and and deep down they know that this is probably the last time they'll ever put on a helmet. And those conversations are very very hard. And then they there's other conversations where you know you're saying goodbye, but that person's going to get claimed. And and then there's conversations where it's like we want you back on the practice squad. You're still part of our team. And um you know, so each one is different. Um they're all still very difficult because ultimately you know they every player you your dream is to play in the NFL and uh so it never gets easier. >> Yeah. Like as an example Xavier Restrepo is is on your practice squad and he could be a player away from being on the active roster. >> Well well they all are. You know like I've said I've said before they're really the next 16. You know it's uh every player you know the NFL doesn't have three and four deep. It's really a two deep. Uh and then you have guys who are kind of playing multiple positions to make it a three deep. Um you know, we go up on game day with eight offensive linemen. I mean, that's you technically you're not too deep at every position. There's guys who have to flex and be able to play multiple positions, but those guys on the next 16, they're they're next up. If someone gets hurt, they're they're being pulled up. So they're next on the depth chart. So they're every bit a part as part of the team. They're in every meeting. They're working out with the team. They're um they're in practice with the team. They're just not dressing on game day. Um that and obviously the salary is a little different, but they're they're every bit a part of this football team as as the next man. >> I think that a lot of fans really enjoyed the message that Mike Borggoni and you gave Truman Jones that he was on the Tennessee Titans active roster. I know those are some of your favorite moments. >> Oh, yeah. because there there's a that's a young man who's been battling for a few years trying to make the roster and uh >> you know sometimes it you know >> every situation is different and sometimes players need the right situation and not every situation that we walk into is good for the player. Um this happened to be one of those situations where getting his hand in the dirt, getting him going vertical, just thinking about one thing and one thing only. That's setting edges and and get well getting after the passer and setting your edge on the way there. But uh and he's really he's really taken a big jump this off season. He still has a ways to go like we've talked about, but uh but he's definitely heading in the right direction and like I told him, we'll never say no to a pass rusher. >> Yeah, of course. And he he flashes a bunch. You know, going into training camp there, I'm sure there are ideas of of who's going to start, who's going to back up guys, but then based on play, things change. and right guard Fernando Carmona, rookie that comes into the National Football League. At least I think for a lot of us off of the field, he's one of those guys that use training camp and use the preseason to prove he should be the starter at right guard. What are your thoughts about what he did? >> Go back to OTAAS, too. You know, just uh being relentless in the playbook. I know we didn't get a lot of chance. OTAAS aren't set up for big guys to show what they've got, but uh you can see his process. You can see his mental horsepower. uh than him taking advantage of training camp. You know, it wasn't uh I'd be lying to you if I said that we're going into training camp thinking that we're going to give him an opportunity. Thought we were in pretty good shape right there, but um after a couple weeks, you're like, "Shoot, let's just see what he has." And to his credit, you know, once he wedged his foot in the door, he's like, "This thing ain't closing." And uh uh he did a really nice job. He's attacked it. And again, like like everyone else, he has a long way to go. He hasn't got it yet, but um uh he's going to see some different body types. He's going to see some elite football players. I know he sees one every every day in uh in Jeffrey Simmons, but um every week you're uh he's going to see the best of the best of the best and and it's going to be a challenge for him, but we're confident that he's going to attack that challenge. >> What do you think of the rookies in general, coach, through training camp, preseason, as you get ready for the real thing? They've all improved and you know like um you know I I was I was talking to I forget who I was talking to yesterday but uh you know I'd mentioned that you know the the average age of the NFL rookie is is older than it used to be. >> But the but the rookies we drafted are very very young. You look at uh Carnell, he's 20 I think he's 21. He is >> uh Kendrick Faulk is the youngest player in the entire NFL. Anthony Hill is only 21. Um, uh, uh, uh, Singleton is I think he's 21. I think he is, but like we're just a young young young group. And, um, and so you look at the overall rookies, and I'll just speak for the first three, they've all gotten better. M uh they've all improved in their craft. I know uh Kellrick got hurt uh the last two weeks, but he was ascending at a at a at a pretty good pace uh to the point where we feel really good about him and the direction he's going and the type of player we have there. Uh they're only going to get stronger. They're only going to get faster. They're only going to get more experience and the what and and I know it's boring and I keep saying it, but what what you see today is their floor and and they're only going to get better. >> And you're saying that about the entire team? really the entire team. >> Yeah. I mean, it's a young team. It's one of the youngest teams in the National Football League. And I'm sure that's that's the message to all Titans fans is we're going out there to win immediately, but this thing is going to get better. >> Yeah. Whatever it is on Sunday, I promise you it'll be better the next week and the week after. Like, it's we we've got a good group of men. Um they're they're made of the right stuff. Uh athletic, explosive. Um it's just going to be time on task and reps. And we are we're going in full board. We want to win football games. We want to go to the playoffs. We want to win our division. We want to win championships. And uh that that does not change. But our process and getting better, going to bed better than when we woke up, attacking every moment. Um that that won't change. >> And of course in this room, we have a lot of pictures of the late great Coach Mack. He would love to hear that time on task was something he talked about [laughter] all the time. Coach, what is your philosophy on team captains and and how do you uh alert the team of that? Yeah, we're uh we'll have our vote on on Wednesday at the uh during the uh team meeting and um uh you know, usually we have a captain representing each side of the ball. So, offense, defense, and then special teams. And then we'll nominate a fourth captain every week. >> Okay. All right. Well, that'll be a fun uh I'm I'm sure that'll be fun this week. What do you think of the overall leadership of the 2026 Titans? >> I I I love it. You know, like I said, I think this team actually likes each other. You know, like um you know, sometimes uh one, you can look at see it in preseason games, just the amount of joy that the the veterans watching the game had for their uh for the younger guys as they were battling in the third and fourth quarter. Uh everybody, no one sitting on the bench, everyone involved in the game. Uh which I thought was uh which is a a a demonstration of uh love and regard for your teammate. But um but just going through these exit meetings with the guys that we were releasing, it's you know, they're they genuinely love that locker room. You know, the the the the guys have a good bond. Um coming in the next day, it was very somber. Like a lot of those position rooms were disappointed that some of their guys uh were let go and that they weren't in the room anymore. And it's, like I said, it's never easy. Uh but I do think this locker room really enjoys being around each other. I think they all enjoy the work they put in. I don't think anyone looks at another player in the locker room and says, "Man, this guy's stealing a free meal. This guy's stealing a meal because he just shows up to work to punch a a paycheck." I think our guys work deliberately. Um, and like I said, I I can look to a man. I don't think there's a single man in our locker room that's trying to take a shortcut. They're trying to figure out how to get better and they're attacking every moment. And I think that that builds trust. It builds appreciation. Um, and it uh and it makes you want to play for your partner. >> Builds wins too, doesn't it? >> Of course it does. Yeah. God willing. Anyway, >> yeah. Um, and I know that all Titans fans off of last season want to know more about Jeff Simmons and Cam Ward. They've kind of been the leaders of the team, at least last year, they were going into the offseason. What are your thoughts about them? >> Yeah, you know, I I feel like I don't know I don't know Jeff before I got here. Um, but what I see is a man who's done everything the right way. Um, the the way he speaks to his teammates, um, and I feel like he's taken a jump. you know, you I I think he's really approached this season probably a little bit differently than he has in the past. I don't know that. It's it's going off what I've been told, but uh but he checks every single box when you talk about on the field work ethic, on the field language, off the- field language, off the- field work ethic, the way he takes care of his body. I mean, the his work in the community, um just the the all-around man that he is, um you can't ask for a better better leader. And then you talk about Cam on the other side. Um, you know, he's he's growing into his shoes. You know, he's still just a secondyear kid trying to figure it out. And, uh, but he's got he checks all the boxes of work ethic and all the intangibles that you want out of the quarterback position. Um, but there's a lot of guys on both sides of the ball and really all three phases that are deserving of of being a captain. You know, you Ridley does a great job as a veteran voice in the uh receiver room. He's shown up every day um all the way across the board on the offensive line. But um and then on the D line, like on the defense, like that Dline room is filled with alpha males. Uh guys who just work relentlessly. Um linebacker room. Cody's been a a leader for a long time, not just here, but everywhere he's been. and uh Cedric's taken a big step and the safety I mean all the way across the board there's examples of tremendous leaders on this football team and uh we may name captains but that doesn't mean that everyone can't serve and lead one another and that's that's what's exciting about this group. >> I love you going through your mind going through each position and and thinking about all the leaders that you have on this team. title: Will the Pittsburgh Steelers give Joey Porter Jr. a new contract? | Pro Football Talk | NFL on NBC
text: One factor that would help the Steelers in that game is if Joey Porter Jr. would find his way back to the field. He's not injured. He was on the pup list for all of training camp in the preseason. He's not injured. Passed the physical last week. He could have passed the physical day one. This was a hold in. And it's obvious it was a hold in. Mike McCarthy has addressed it multiple times. It's a hold in. It's business. Porter wants a new contract. Porter's in this very rare position of being essentially a first round pick because he was the 32nd overall selection in 2023, but he was in round two because the first round that year only had 31 picks thanks to the Dolphins tampering situation with Shawn Peyton. Tom Brady lost the first round pick. The Steelers who acquired what would have been the Bears first pick in round two. That was the Chase Clayool trade that gave the Steelers that spot. They take Porter. He has three years. He's due to make, I think, about three or four million this year. Due to be a free agent or tag next year, but he wants his reward and he's been waiting for it. And thanks to the Steelers outdated policy that says no new contracts after the season begins puts a lot of pressure on both sides to get it done this week. If they don't get it done this week and the Steelers stick to their outdated policy, they're not getting it done until after the season. Period. No matter what. Well, if they don't get it done this week and he decides not to play, when's he going to play? He's not getting a deal. When's he gonna play? The extra factor here is that Porter's dad, Joey, was an accomplished player primarily in Pittsburgh. And the way I hear it, Joey Senior's driving this bus, which could make Joey Junior's resolve even stronger than it otherwise would be. You know, usually it's just player, agent, and family. And the family doesn't have any experience in the business. So, at some point, the agent gets an offer. And for most agents, the calculation is simple. Would I advise my son, brother, nephew to take this? Somebody in my in my family tree, would I tell them, "You should take this. This is too good to pass up." The factor here with Joey Porter Jr.'s his father knowing the business, knowing how the sausage gets made, he's been part and parcel of the NFL as a player, as an assistant coach. If he says that's not good enough, then that's not good enough. It kind of reminds me of Derell Rivas when his uncle Shawn Gilbert was giving him some very pointed advice during his protracted hold out with the Jets some 16 years ago. So, a showdown could be looming in Pittsburgh. It could get ugly. What do you do when a player under contract refuses to play? It's a oneperson wildcat strike. What does the team do? The team has rights under the CBA. The team has the ability to play hard ball with the player. What do you do? Could you trade him? I'm told there haven't been any phone calls to the Steelers about possibly trading for Porter, paying him 30 million plus per year, giving up whatever the Steelers would be looking for by way of trade. I'm told the phone hasn't been ringing. What do you do? It's been of all the holdins this year, the one that has been talked about the least, but it's going to come into focus sharply this week if they don't get a deal done. Is it as simple as Porter wants it to start with a three and the Steelers are willing to start with a two? I think it's more than 29 versus 30 million. I think there's a large gap there. I think that the Steelers value Porter one way. Porter values himself a very different way. And what we've seen in the quarterback market in recent years, and I think this is a product of when the market stays depressed for a while, and this happened with the quarterback market in 2018, it had been depressed for several years. The market at the quarterback position was not going up at the rate the salary cap was going up, at the rate other positions were going up. When it finally started to move, the next guy to get a contract became the highest paid player at the position. And it went one after another after another. It was Jimmy Garoppolo to Kirk Cousins to Matthew Stafford to Matt Ryan. It was boom boom boom a little bit more, a little bit more, a little bit more. That's been happening in the cornerback market starting with Patrick Certain. And there have been, you know, JC Horn and a little bit more and a little bit more. And now Devin Witherspoon has moved to 33 million per year. Porter may be thinking, "All right, 331, 335, 34 for me." Steelers aren't thinking that way. That's the problem. And again, the other problem is if we don't have a deal by week one, Steelers policy. Sorry, that's our policy. Why do you do it? I don't know. It was like that when I got here. That's our policy. There's no offramp. There's no endgame. Now, I was talking to somebody about this yesterday. There is a way that the Steelers could craft an exception along the lines of, well, once a player plays his first game of the season, there's no further negotiation. So, if Porter would skip week one, the season hasn't started for him. That's an easy way to get around the handcuffs you've applied to yourself with this ridiculously outdated policy. And they know it. They know it's outdated. They know it. They refused to change it. Flip side, we'll know within the next day or two whether or not Christian Gonzalez is the Patriots cornerback who's in the same situation as Porter, but that's the the hold in on and off maybe sort of kind of holdin. The hold in that no one wants to call a holdin. Kind of like what was going on in San Francisco with Christian McCaffrey. Oh. Oh, sorry. Sorry, 49ers beat Writers. I know you get triggered when we point that out, but hey, guys want to get paid. And as I learned last year in the Michael Parson situation, when you have played football for 20 years, there is an injury somewhere on your body that keeps you from feeling fully confident about going out and playing. Hey, Joey Porter Jr. could try that. If it does get ugly, sorry, back's tight. Sorry, knees stiff. What do you do? How ugly do you want to make it? So with Christian Gonzalez, who was injured or injured for a couple of weeks and then came back to practice, he won't commit to playing week one. He won't commit to it. What does that tell you? I mean, usually the answer to the question is, "What are you talking about? Of course I'm playing. I'm on the team. I'm under contract. He's under contract two more years. Of course I'm playing." Any hesitation means eh? Tune in, find out. We thought it was going to be easy. It's the same firm that represents Deon Witherspoon. Get that deal done. Witherspoon sets the new record and then Gonzalez beats it. Nope. There's still is this talk that Gonzalez wants a three-year extension and the Patriots holding firm at four. I'm told it's going to be four when it gets done. It will be four. So the dollars and the structure become very important and they just haven't they haven't been able to work it out and we're two days away from the first game and the Patriots could use him. You got Jackson Smith and Jigma. You got Rasheed Shahed who's had a whole off season training camp and preeason to get properly integrated into the new Brian Flory offense in Seattle. You don't have Christian Gonzalez. You got a problem if you're New England, especially since the Seattle running game is a work in progress. No, Zack Charbanet, Jadarian Price, first round pick expected to carry the load. How's that going to go? We don't know. They don't know. They may be dialing up a lot of passes and maybe they skew pass heavy if they find out 90 minutes before kickoff Gonzalez isn't going to play. And I think it's going to come down to that. I think it's going to be 90 minutes before kickoff. Will he be active? Will he be inactive? There's a strategic reason to keeping the cards close to the vest, but I really do think the Patriots won't know until we get down to the final hour and a half. And Gonzalez may not know, but we've got two guys, two corners, two potential holdins who may cite some injury that the team will have no choice but to accept as legitimate. Number one, it's a bad PR look when you say, "Ah, he's not really injured. He's mingering." But this is a direct product of the holdin dynamic. It's too expensive to hold out. the consequences are too great for the player. The the league through the most recent CBA got to the point where it's virtually impossible for a guy to say, "I'm not showing up." And it's much easier to show up, not practice or maybe practice some and then you're injured and then as the season approaches, I'm not playing without my contract. One of these days there's going to be a showdown. One of these days, someone's going to either overplay his hand from the players perspective or the team is going to decide, hey, enough of this. Maybe at the urging of the management council, enough of this. No more of this. You show up, you're under contract, you play. And you get your new contract. If you get your new contract, the team has various rights available to it under the CBA. One of these days, somebody is going to use them. Hi, it's Mike Florio. Thanks for watching PFT on YouTube.
